review_text: Excellent food. Cozy ambiance. Friendly staff. The flavorful cuttlefish appetizer is prepared using small embers from the woodfire oven. The pheasant and sea bass were great. The delicious roasted pineapple with mascarpone ice cream is a must have! Prices include tip. Sit in the kitchen-side seats for a great view of all the action!

Like Charlie Bird, the first restaurant from this team, everything here is delicious, service is excellent, and they play good hip hop music.

We only tried a few of the small plates, pizzas and a pasta, but it was all so good that we definitely need to return again soon:

- Pane Carasau ($7)
Instead of starting with bread, these are crisp crackers served with a dollop of ricotta, black pepper and honey. It's not as good as bread, but is a nice little light starter to begin with.

- Charred Cauliflower ($16)
Another much lighter option, if you don't care at all about your health and just want bang for your buck, I would consider ordering the Marinara Pizza instead since it's just $1 more than this small plate of veggies. It was delicious though, and as you will notice with the prices of the items, everything seems a bit on the higher end, due to the fact that they are one of the many restaurants that has now embraced the no tipping policy.

- Margherita Pizza ($18)
Opting for the plain old original Margherita to compare it against other places, this was an incredible rendition. The dough here is amazing, which makes at least one of the pizzas a must order.

- Calzone ($21)
Filled with ricotta, prosciutto and sopressata, this is another excellent option from the pizza section.

- Martelli Spaghetti ($19)
Accompanied by Spanish anchovy and bergamot, the heavy lemony taste was almost too overpowering, but the pasta itself was a perfect texture and did have a ton of flavor. It was on the oily side too, leaving a nice pool in the bowl which would have been nice to eat with some bread. This was good, but it definitely made me wish I tried the Rigatoni with sausage, nettle and smoked ricotta too.

- Pear with Mascarpone Gelato and Hazelnuts ($12)
I would probably skip over this option on a dessert menu, but since it was the single option available, we tried it, and I am very glad we did, because it was excellent. The pear was roasted in the oven, and you could still see it smoking under the refreshing, cool scoop of gelato. The hazelnuts sprinkled on top added a delicious crunch and rounded out a surprisingly satisfying and sweet dessert to end a memorable meal.

The staff was so welcoming and the atmosphere was so nice that it definitely make me want to return sooner than later to try more of the pizzas and maybe some items from the veggies and entrees sections that we didn't even get to touch on this visit.

Just to let everyone in on a little secret my name is not Mario A (Just my Yelp alter ego) it's actually Pasquale A. So being a huge fan Charlie bird and this restaurant restaurant bearing my name I had to try it. I was very impressed from start to finish. First off immediately after sitting down you realize how comfortable it is to eat there the seats are super comfortable. Th restaurant also has an awesome chill unpretentious vibe with as you know coming from the Charlie bird team plays GREAT music.
We wanted a bottle of wine and the manager/somm recommend a Sicilian frappato served slightly chilled it was exactly what we were looking for. 
     Onto the food, excellent! We stated with the winter lettuces and it was so simple and fresh. The vinaigrette tasted like it came from my grandmas cantina great wine flavor. Next up the sepia, super simple but unbelievably flavorful and tender get it!
Onto the pizza I'm a margarita junkie and huge critic when it comes to pizza. It was very good way above average  but in my opinion the food out shined the pizza.
       Next up the wood fired skate wing. Skate is one my favorite fishes to eat and when it's done right it really is one of the more enjoyable fishes out there. Prepared with the bone in which is a little unusual for skate  but I loved it. Super moist and flavorful. 
    And now dessert. They only had one dessert for the day and it's all they needed. A wood charred pear with a super delicious fior de latte gelato finished with sea salt and evoo. It was so good that my girlfriend and I had to order another one. Sweet,savory, cold, warm, soft, crunchy it was honestly great please leave that one on the menu!
    Over all a really great experience can't wait to go back! Big W for all the Pasquales out there!

Where do I start ?!? This past week I was reading Time Out magazine and I read about Pasquale Jones opening. The restaurant is near where I live so I booked marked and told myself "I will try that asap" 

We just went tonight for dinner! They have been very busy and I totally understand why. Cheers to Chef Ryan Hardy. The food is outstanding. I literally couldn't stop eating!!!! 

We had a reservation for 8:30pm but got there 10 minutes before. They were running late but the service was so great that I didn't might waiting for our table. They pored us prosecco while waiting as a courtesy. 

When we finally sit down we had one of their pizzas, rigatoni pasta (I would said this one was a bit salty but I believe it was because of the sausage) and charred cauliflower. Everything tasted perfect. I could stay there eating for another hour. 

Dessert was also very good. As I heard they will only have one dessert choice every night. I was very lucky because they had one of my favorite fruits(pineapple) and ice cream. It was incredible good!! 

Since we were siting at the bar we saw many dishes been prepare. They cook everything from scratch. We had an amazing wine and the service was great! 

Well, 5 stars to Chef Hardy and his crew. Everything was amazing. I would definitely come back for the pork shoulder !!! Can't wait ...

Was excited to come here based off of a review from a trusted source. Arrived on a Friday at around 7:30 and was not acknowledged for about 5 minutes as two hosts helped a couple in front of us. Once the host addressed us, we were told that the wait would be around 2 hours but it also could be less since they were still figuring out their flow. Obviously waiting 2 hours is never ideal..but we were willing to wait it out for great food and wine. Strange though since half the restaurant at this time was empty. Put our name down and were told that they would text us when the table was available. 

We went to a cocktail bar to wait..and wait...after 2 hours and 30 mins we were back with no text and the host was extremely surprised to see us. Strangely enough the restaurant was packed now so either people had made reservations in advance or other people were seated before us. At this time at party of 3 left whose table we easily could have been seated at. "You guys are very prompt..unfortunately it may be about 30 more minutes..but it just 2 guys eating so they may be faster." So the wait was actually 3 hours or more..who knows though cause decided to just cut our losses and leave. I would have been fine if the host had been a bit better at estimating the time (an hour off is a bit absurd) or just been a bit more accommodating but I definitely can't tolerate this lack of awareness and service. Maybe it's cause they don't care about tips here. Figure it out guys...

This place is just fabulous.  Have been here twice now and the kitchen is already in high gear, turning out delicious food.  I find the setting super comfortable.  Those chairs!  Wow, super comfy.  Everything I have tried on the menu is great.  So many highlights.  Clam pie, calzone, braised leeks and fresh pastas.  Wine service by Grant Reynolds is superlative.  Great geeky wine list.  Tax and tip are included in the menu prices.  A tremendous addition to the NYC dining scene.

No doubt Pasquale Jones is good.  I was not quite as impressed as I hoped, especially compared to Charlie Bird; however, I enjoyed the experience immensely.  

The pizza is great.  Luckily, when I went, they had a truffle pizza special.  Oh my god, I actually thought I was having an orgasm while I consumed each cheesy, crispy, truffly bite.  This should totally be a regular menu item.  While the clam pizza was very good, I didn't find it destination worthy.  

The rigatoni was pretty disappointing.  The meat was tasty, but the pasta itself was not worth consuming. 

Like Charlie Bird, the wine selection is excellent.  The staff is extremely knowledgeable and helped us select something that paired perfectly with our food and was exactly what we were looking for.

The space is a bit cramped but the decor is welcoming.  Moreover, I did not find the music selection to be quite Charlie Bird level either, but maybe that's just my love of 90s hip hop talking.
Incredible. Ricotta, clam pizza, and skate wing were all fantastic. Need to return for the pork shank for two.

4 food snobs thoroughly enjoyed our meal in this small, newish restaurant.  We had a lovely server, enjoyed the fresh, well prepared food and the wine was also great.
Highlights are the beet salad (one of the best ever), leeks, tortelloni, and the steak. The food is all flavorful, seasoned well and tastes healthy. 
Honestly this is one of the best meals we've had from start to finish in a long time.  Prices include tip, and from  the quality of the food to the service, it's reasonably priced.

I'm so hesitant to write a review because it's hard enough to get into this place but alas, I'm all about giving credit where credit is due. I made a 6:00 reservation for Sunday night a few weeks in advance. It's a tradition of ours to have pizza and pasta every Sunday and our local place just wasn't cutting it. We almost cancelled because we were having a case of the couch potato Sundays but we rallied and made the trek down from HK. When we walked in right on time we were very warmly greeted by the lovely Hostesses. The atmosphere is so serene, the music is playing at the perfect level, the place was completely full but there was no deafening roar like most NYC restaurants. We were seated at the perfect little booth for 2 on the left when you walk in and another huge thumbs up that we actually had quite a bit of space between us and the table next to us. The service is a group effort and it was absolutely spot on, not overbearing and not absent, just right. The Somm was not only totally hot :) but was very accommodating.  We went with a bottle of Red from Sicily that was pretty classic for the area. Their wine list is not as robust as Charlie Bird's but it's interesting, well thought out and has quite a few selections under $60.00. On to the food!! We started with the braised leeks, ignoring my BF's displeasure but who was the one that was licking the bowl? This is a must order. We then chose the Coppa pie which would have been perfect if it was cooked just a smidge longer, but then again, we like our pies almost burnt on the bottle. Next up was the rigatoni with sausage that was out.of.this.world.order it. We also went with a side of charred broccoli rabe that made you forget that it was a plate of vegetables. For dessert they offer one thing, grilled pineapple with gelato which sounds pretty meh but let me warn you, you will want like 10 bowls of this...unbelievable flavors! We had such a perfect experience that I booked the same table for next Sunday...this is definitely our new Sunday night dinner spot. It's kinda a good thing there's a little travel involved all the way from Hells' Kitchen because if Pasquale Jones was any closer, we'd be there every night.

Currently only serving Beer and Wine.
Rigatoni was decent as was the clam pizza if a bit salty. Side are quite good but not big enough to share with more than 2 people.
Biggest disappointment was the $125 steak. Would normally never order this however there were 6 of us and 3 were in no carb mode.  If I think of the other steaks in this price range this one doesnt come close.  They have to take this off the menu.  Its just not worth it and is a very strange addition as pizza and pastas are a much lower price point.
Certainly not a destination place.

Food is ok with small portions (pizza portion was fine).  We got the white asparagus, which was good but only two pieces for $20. Charred cauliflower was fine. Also got the pasta (can't remember the name but the last one on the menu with sage and pancetta), that was pretty good but small portion as well. Margarita pizza was mediocre. Alcohol portions are TINY - got less than half a glass of prosecco. When we asked him why it was so small, he said it was the way they pour it. He did top us off a bit, which was nice, but still a little ridiculous. If you still insist on trying this place, get a bottle. It's much more cost efficient. Gratuity is included within the menu so don't need to tip.

We scored an early dinner res here when our client came to town and it was the perfect spot for a delicious dinner!

The place is small, but cute and doesn't feel crowded or squished like other NY restaurants. They play rap/hip hop music (but not blasting), which I thoroughly enjoyed. 

In terms of food: 

Warm ricotta is LIFE. So yummy and fresh. You MUST get this. 

In terms of other apps, the cuttlefish was pretty tasty, but I'd skip the charred cauliflower (was just okay and had a lot going on). 

Clam pizza and Margherita pizza were both on point. I actually preferred to classic Margherita to everything else. They just did it so well and you can't beat a brick oven pizza. 

Staff is really great - attentive, but not annoying, and they can make good recommendations on food and wine. 

I will definitely be back again. My only wish was that they had more wines by the glass. We enjoyed what we had, but selection was limited unless you wanted to take a chance on a bottle.

Shama-lama-ding-dong, this was good.

New to the neighborhood, Pasquale (pronounced Pas-kwal-leh) Jones is brought to you by the group responsible for Charlie Bird on King Street, and I have to say, everything was excellent, just like my experience at Charlie Bird. The space, while a little small, is pretty modern, intimate, and chic, and the open kitchen with the two huge wood-fired ovens was a pretty cool sight. They apparently take reservations on Resy, but after checking for the last 2 weeks, it didn't seem like there was that much availability, so we decided to show up early and then if the wait wasn't too bad, we'd go elsewhere for a drink then head back. We arrived at 6pm, and was told there was about a 45-minute wait, which we expected. We went elsewhere for a drink, then they texted us 15 minutes before the previously mentioned seating time, so we had time to pay our tabs and head over. We were eventually seated at the bar, which gave us a front row seat into the kitchen.

The two of us (aka I) decided to go for broke and order something from each of the menu sections: Little Neck clam white pizza, pappardelle with braised short rib and reggiano, and the pork shank with fingerling potatoes for two. The Little Neck clam pizza was perfect, as the crust was just the right amount of crispiness to chewiness, and the white sauce and lemon were a perfect complement to clams on top. The wood-fired oven really makes a difference, in my opinion. The pappardelle had a really nice chew, but the braised short rib was slightly mushier than I personally like with pasta. Still very delicious and tasty dish, but probably my least favorite out of everything. Yet, if that's the least successful dish they have to offer, you're in good shape.

But, the pork shank. Holy cow (pig). We watched them take the shank out of the oven, give it a good sear, and then finish it off in the oven, adding the potatoes and garnishes, and then pouring the juices back on top.  Again, it was cool to see everything made in front of us, and it sort of made us appreciate it a little more. Anyways, the pork shank was crispy on the outside with that nice sear on the outside, and the tender, slightly fatty meat inside was the perfect texture and fattiness. Easily my favorite part of the meal. You'd think that a pork shank would be a relatively commonplace dish to make, especially with all of the talented chefs in New York City, but it's hard to find it exactly the way I like it, and they executed perfectly here. 

We finished off the meal with the only dessert they had on the menu, which was roasted pineapple chunks with mascarpone gelato, olive oil, and chopped roasted almonds. The roasted pineapple had just the right amount of moisture, the mascarpone gelato had this tartness that all worked quite well with the crunch of the almonds and sourness of the pineapple. One of the better desserts I've had in recent memory, and if they ever decide to expand the dessert menu, the outlook is very good for that.

Service was excellent, and kept the refills and the food coming at a very nuanced pace. The chefs, even when busy, were very interactive, welcoming, and friendly. Like many restaurants these days, Pasquale Jones has gratuity included in all of their pricing, so there's no need to tip. For all the food that we got (sans drinks), it came out to less than $60 per person, which ain't half bad, so the value is definitely there.

Overall, we had an excellent time, and I think Pasquale Jones is a great addition to the neighborhood. Everyone asks me to compare it to Charlie Bird, but while the concepts are similar, I just think Pasquale Jones is a great restaurant on its own, and it's worth evaluating standalone. I'd definitely recommend it for a small group or a date (with a flexible schedule). I was told that next time I needed to order the braised leeks, as well as try the red pie, although I would easily come back again just for that pork shank. Regardless of my future dining options, I will definitely be back soon.

New in a familiar setting , excellent interior design , and creative cooking combined with personal and attentive service. 
Small menu , good wine list. Seasonal starters it seems (March: white asparagus, leeks) plus some staple pizzas. 
Prices are more than ok for this location and already incl your tip.

Stopped in on our way home from an already long night out of restaurant bouncing. Have been hearing a lot about the place. All good so had to pop in. Only orders one margarita pie since we were already full but we passed by and had to try something. The pie was very good perfect crisp and char. Cheese and sauce both worked well on the margarita pie. 
Would I come into the city and pass up Lucali for it? No way but if your in the are and you can't make Lucalis time requirements then it's definitely worth a taste. I can't wait to come back on an empty stomach and try some of their entrees. 
Friendly waiter. 
Great music. Old school rap.

Loved our meal at Pasquale Jones! Came on a Tuesday night with a few friends. We shared several dishes but below are our favorites:

- roasted leek appetizer 
- peashoot pizza with lemon
- little neck clam pizza 

Menu changes often to include seasonal flavors. Friendly staff and knowledge sommelier. Can't wait to go back soon!

Really enjoyed dinner here.  Service and wine were great.  Food was very good. We had the cuttlefish, white asparagus, rigatoni with sausage, clam pizza (a little too salty) and the only dessert that was being offered- grilled pineapple and marscapone gelato which was amazing! Lovely, casual atmosphere, will definitely be back to try other things on the menu :-)

Great restaurant, amazing service and cozy environment! The food was pretty good, but more vegetarian options would have been appreciated. However, the brick ovens made it so warm and friendly, and we were surprised to see that the tip was already included for a party of two! Highly recommend this spot.

We went there at the opening and this place is great. Pizzas and pastas were great. The atmosphere and the service were nice. However it seems impossible to book a table even using their website and every time we try to go back, there is a 1h wait. Would love to go back but they got to start using other way to take reservation

Part 2- went there in person and manage to get a reservation late on Sunday. The farfalle with java bean and prosciutto were delicious. I wished they put more since I was really tempted to get a second plate. The TIP is included which is always nice!! Will come back but will order more food

We walked in here on a Tuesday evening and were hoping to get seated relatively quickly as they don't take reservations.  The restaurant is intimate and has an open kitchen concept so it can get a bit warm but overall the modern feel is great.  

I liked that the menu was simple and easy to pick from as the restaurant targets dishes they are good at.  We tried the leak appetizer that came with parmigiano and walnuts for some good texture and flavors.  We then tried the Margherita and Diavola pizzas, both fresh and well done which we enjoyed.  To wrap things up, we tried the only thing on the menu, rhubarb with mascarpone ice cream, pistachios and olive oil for another well balanced and textured dish!

Overall, the service was friendly, ambiance was inviting and food was good.  This is another restaurant that includes tipping so prices may seem a bit more 'inflated' but you don't have to worry about tipping which is nice.  I look forward to coming back. 

Buon appetito.

The menu isn't too extensive, which I liked. It listed a bunch of eye catching stuff that I wanted to try. I was also happy to see escarole make an appearance here in the greens section (though I didn't get to try it out).

We tried three starters: pane carasau, cuttlefish and sugar snap peas. All were good, but slightly small in terms of portion size for the price point. While this is a "no tipping" restaurant and one should expect higher pricing, I felt that they went a bit too far. Based on my accounting of things, I'd say they are charging about 40-50% more per item. If you figure a 20% tip into the math, then you're still overpaying by 20-30%, depending on the particular item in question. So while the idea of a no tipping restaurant may seem great, the real loser is the customer, who can no longer adjust their tip downward for low food quality or poor service. Our waiter was kind of a dick, and I wasn't super impressed with the food either. As such, I felt like I over-payed for several aspects of the meal.

The pane carasau is essentially what you might get for free in a bread basket at a high end Italian joint or a place like Quality Italian. It was really just thin, crispy bread chips with a small dollop of delicious, warm honey and black pepper ricotta. $9.

The cuttlefish was steep at $18 for the plate. The pickled peppers on top were a nice hit of heat, and it was cooked nicely in terms of texture, with only a slight bit of it being, perhaps, a bit overcooked and chewy. It tasted clean, though, and the charcoal grilling method added a nice earthy ash flavor to it.

The snap pea dish with watercress and cream was probably the best of the three, but, again, extremely overpriced at $17. The peas carried a nice sweetness, but I was hoping for more cream.

Now for the pizza (category 1: full pies only, no slices available). We tried two pies: little neck clam and the special pizza of the day, which was a morel mushroom and cheese pie. The clam pie had good flavor, but it felt a little sparse on the actual clams and toppings. That means the diner feels ripped off when paying $24 for six small slices. That's a hell of a profit margin when you think about how cheap it is to make this shit!

The morel pizza could have used more toppings a bit closer to the edge of the crust. That wasted real estate also translates to the feeling of being ripped off when the bill comes. This was, however, the better of the two pies, in my opinion. The morels had a meaty quality to them, and a good amount of earthiness.

On the pasta angle, we went with the baby goat pappardelle. This was a delicious dish. The meat was very tender, and the pasta was well dressed with sauce. The texture of the pasta was just right. While the portion size felt a little bit small for $23, I didn't mind as much because it was top notch quality.

For the meats, we tried two dishes: pork shank for two, and dry aged rib eye for two. 

Let's start with the pork. This was delicious. While a bit small for two, the price of $48 wasn't too bad. Well, I mean, when you compare it to the outstanding crackling pork shank with firecracker apple sauce at Maloney & Porcelli, which only costs $36 and can feed two people with extra to bring home, then, yeah, it's way overpriced here. But given all else on the menu, I felt this was probably the best bargain. The flavors were outstanding and it had hints of sausage spice from the fennel and rosemary. This is a must-order if you decide to come here.

You can pass on the rib eye, however. It definitely delivered on the dry-aged flavor, but it was very small for two people to share at $125. If I had to guess, I'd say this was about 22oz on the bone. Maybe 24oz. For that size steak at a steakhouse, you pay between $50 and $60. So here, I would have expected to pay about $75 to account for the tip being included. At $125, we are looking at a massive fucking mark-up.

Contrast this with the best rib eye in Manhattan over at Osteria Morini, just around the corner, which offers a steak that's more than twice the size of this thing at 52oz, with 120 days of dry-aging flavor, and accompanied by two generously-sized sides for just $145. Uhh... no brainer. Anyway, this steak had a bit of chew to it. Not as tender as we had hoped and expected from dry-aging.

It was cooked perfectly to medium rare, and it had a great crust on the outside. The crispy meat surrounding the bone was excellent as well. However there was no rib cap to speak of. Perhaps it was butchered off for some other use. 7/10.

The steak came with a nice roasted onion. And something came with a side of citrus-dressed arugula.

But the highlight of the night, aside from the pork shank, was seeing Michael J. Fox and Dennis Leary in the dining room, eating together with their wives.

To sum up: skip this place unless you are focused on the pork shank. If that's not your thing, then stick with the pizza and pasta, but I, personally, would still go elsewhere. 2.5 *

This place started off great. Our first visit is March was amazing. We had the clam pizza and then proceeded to watch maybe 10 orders of the rib eye come out. Super jealous so on our next trip on early April we ordered the rib eye for two and it was amazing. Pretty much the best steak I had ever had. I would basically wax poetic about how great the rib eye was to friends and we ended up bringing another couple back two weeks later. Of course we ordered the rib eye and this time it was just sub par. Good but not great- clearly the cut of meat was not as great as just a couple weeks before. Disappointing for sure but I didn't want to write it off just yet. Well, we came back last night with friends to try to again and this time it was awful. The worst cut of rib eye you can imagine. Half was pure fat. For $125 it was a complete rip off. We had a pile of fat on the dish and I had to mention it to our server. I mean it was disgusting. 

I can't actually believe the kitchen thought it was acceptable to send out. So sad because in just one month the quality of this place has dropped so dramatically. I thought it was on track to being one off the best new restaurants in the city this year and told everyone I could about it. While the pasta and pizzas are still good, the fact that they think it's acceptable to drop the quality of their meat so dramatically is incredibly disappointing.

Would not recommend or go back (After having gone back 4x in 2 months)

So disappointed in the rapid decline in quality of product here.

This place is so good.. Charlie Bird but even better. Get the charred cauliflower, the little neck clam pizza, margherita pizza, and the sunchoke tortellini.  It was all amazing.. Reservations are a must. Get there asap

A great casual, chic pizza, Italian joint.  The menu is fairly short, but the items are not your usual pizza joint dishes.   We sat at the bar and enjoyed watching the chefs at work.   I think the menu items change often, so most likely not all of the dishes will be available again.  I really enjoyed the sweet pea salad with mint and watercress.   I'm going to have to try to replicate that at home.  The gnocchi with mushrooms and herbs in some kind of cream sauce was phenomenal. The gnocchi had more of a mashed potato consistency, so that was a bit unexpected, but I liked the change.  All the components of the dish just came together perfectly.  It tasted rustic yet luxurious at the same time.  The last dish was the octopus spaghetti with stinging nettle.  That was just just okay in comparison to the gnocchi.   Interestingly, the dishes came one at a time, like a tasting menu.   I guess we are suppose to share each dish?   
Anyway, the space is really comfortable yet chic, and the music was great, too.  It was an enjoyable experience overall.

This was going to be a 3 star review but I changed it to 4 due to the quality of the food. At the end of the day that's what matters and the food here was exceptional. Although, if I were running a business I would do a better job to make sure that the hostess was friendlier. I understand that the space is small and that you don't want people standing around waiting and cramping people's dining experience but you don't have to rude about it! We did have to wait 2.5 hours on a weekday night for our table, as was semi expected. Our table still had some remains of the previous diners food on my chair and our table. However, at the end of the day the food was very solid here. I tried the leek and also the warm ricotta appetizers, both were solid. The spicy pizza, gnocchi and pig pastas that were all delicious as well. I would definitely recommend this place and hopefully your experience with the service is a bit more pleasant.

The food was ok but the service needs to be worked on. 

I was very excited to try Pasquale Jones because I enjoyed my dining experiences at Charlie Bird. Did a walk-in instead of a reservation. Our waitress rushed and pressured us to put in our orders. Threw down the check before giving us the dessert menu. The atmosphere was that we were at a diner and needed to get in and out asap. 

As for the food, the little neck clam pizza and spaghetti with blue crab were good. The dough of the pizza reminds me of naan bread. The sugar snap pea, speck & apricots, broccoli rabe and asparagus were fine. Nothing really stood out but decent. 

As an FYI, they only serve beer and wine, no full bar. 

Wish we enjoyed it more. The service is a deterrent.
We had the most incredible food here...best we've had since Italy.  Chef Emily Chapman and staff have absolutely nailed it!

Had to wait over an hour for a table on a Friday night, so worth it.  While waiting we walked around little Italy as the streets were blocked off.  

We had a special truffle white pizza that was amazing. The rabbit pastas was also amazing!  They're able to split a lot of wine bottles if you're only in the mood for a few glasses. Pretty solid wine selection as well.

We had reservations for 4pm on Saturday at 8:30pm. We showed up a little early so we walked around Little Italy. to kill time. The other couple actually ended up canceling at the last minute so we showed up at 8:30pm and notified the hostess that it was only 2 now. Not sure if the hostess was stressed but she was extremely condescending and not personable to us at all.  She mentioned that it would be another 1.5 for a table for 2. I get it. We are a two-top now so they want to utilize the four-top for 4 people. But i was just totally put off by her attitude and her unwillingness to act like they want our business now. We told her we would just leave and not even a goodbye. Needless to say we will never be eating at Pasquale Jones and we wont be recommending either.

Excellent service, house made pasta, fresh ingredients cooked with soul, what more could you want? The roast chicken was moist with nice layered flavors. The pizza crust was light and flavorful. The broccoli rabe was savory, just short of bitter and the baby asparagus was cooked perfectly with just the right snap. We spoke to the chef who said they pay top dollar for the best eggs to make their pasta. Prices are very reasonable considering the cost of the high quality ingredients they use. 

The wine list is good and because they were out of the wine we ordered they bumped us up to a better bottle at the same price.

We will most definitely be back.

Went with a party of 5 on a Friday night at 630. Had to wait about an hour but there's a nice bar next door to kill time at. 

Overall, it's pretty in line with all of the new pizza/wine bars like Upland, Covina, etc. Got an octopus special app, snap peas, cuttlefish to start- snap peas were a surprising favorite. 

For entrees we got the clam pizza and margarita pizza, tortellini and chicken. All were good though would probably bypass the pasta and chicken next time and just go with the pizza. Way better value and more enjoyable too. 

Will be back but probably just stick to the pizzas moving forward.

I arrived at Pasquale Jones 5 minutes before they opened. The tall host with blonde hair and glasses opened the door and told me I couldn't  use the restroom, but I could try the restaurant next door... I now wish I would have eaten at the restaurant next door too. 

My boyfriend and I were the second party to be sat. Unfortunately, we weren't even close to one of the first parties to receive food. After seeing countless pizzas leave the kitchen and waiting 50 minutes after ordering, one of the three chefs/owners finally acknowledged that we still hadn't received any food. 

I was then told by our server that the numerous pizzas coming out were for probably for the New York Times photoshoot that was going on. So just know that if there is anything else going on, being a normal customers makes you the last priority. 

By the time our pizza arrived we were over the whole dining experience. The pizza was fine, but for $22 being fine isn't enough. We canceled our last two courses and decided to take our business elsewhere. 

I don't think we will be returning to Pasquale Jones anytime soon.

The food here is delish. We did a walk in and sat at the counter, which i loved as you get to watch the chefs do their magic. Each dish we order was 10/10. Except for the pork shank which was way too salty and we had to send it back. We never send dishes back, but it was on the brink of inedible. I think it was an anomaly because everything else was just so divine. I'll def be back. 
Addicted.

Worst customer service in NYC. Came as part of a party of 2 and was promised a 5-10 minute wait. 25 minutes later and a text with no response, we walk back inside to check on the wait and are told it will take another 25 minutes to get seated.  

How you completely mismanage seating with common day reservation technology is baffling. 5-10 minute wait indicates a party is finishing and paying - this isn't even something you need technology for, just eyes and common sense!

We will absolutely be boycotting this restaurant and recommending friends avoid.  We walked up two blocks and were immediately seated at Emporio and enjoyed a fantastic meal!

Very, very, very good pizza ladies and gents!
The hub and I were lucky enough to come the same evening the NY Times were in to take pics/review. We sat at the bar and couldn't be happier to have a front row seat in front of the action. 

What an impeccable team with such precise execution. We were really impressed with the preparation and the care they took on making a perfect plate. 

The clam pizza is a must try. It's got a rich cream sauce that is making my mouth water thinking about it. I'm lucky that I am actually here again at the restaurant writing this review so I don't have FOMO while I write this. 

The burrata pizza with anchovies is a close second. If you love burrata you will love this pizza. For you are not a fan of tomato sauce, this may not be for you as the anchovies are swimming in ample tomato sauce. 

Lastly, we had the spaghetti with lobster. Pasta was al dente and simply perfection. The portion is a little on the small side but amazing. 

Run over when you can. It's mostly walk-ins. Enjoy!!!

Just last night my pals Vincent and Shawn summoned me to this polished pristine monied operation on the corner of Kenmare And Mulberry, for a late tasting.  The 2 wood fire pizza ovens look like they were designed by Rem Koolhaus, really impressive, but just felt out of place to me. The amount of money that was spent on the joint has me pondering what has happened to Downtown New York City, the place I lived for over 19 years. 

They were running late because Vincent let his metrocard expire and had to wait in a " mad long line" at Yankee Stadium to get a new metrocard (Subway Series postgame, rookie move) , so I ventured into this snazzy new player on the street, and successfully negotiated a table and placed the order. The people that worked there were exceptionally pleasant and professional.  Nice crew. 

I ordered a glass of delicious Barbera and then proceeded to observe the machinations of the restaurants clientelle and I surmised that this is a wall street/hedge fund clubhouse, filled with a lot of trader/broker types that knew each other.  Guessing these fellows bankrolled the joint and now go there and just sort of Douche the place up a bit.  Right next to me was a Patrick Bateman look alike that gave me the creeps.  Kind of brutal.  There were also a few booths of cute girls and slickster guys that were having a great time, eating drinking smoking butts outside.

Smoked Trout Cucumber Salad.  Vincent and Shawn liked it, I didn't try it, not my thing.  

Tajarin (a spaghetti-like noodle) with sweet corn and summer truffle-unique and delish, 2 bites is enough, very delicious I never had anything that tasted quite like that. You gotta have that. 

Clam Pizza - Pretty good not great I'd like bigger chunks of clam and a more thoroughly cooked pie. meh 

Ribeye for 2 cooked in the oven.  Very solid steak.  not as good as Speedy Romeo's however.

The desert was easily the star of the night, berries cooked in the designer pizza oven with gelato and crushed pistachio nuts.  friggin amazing. 

No tipping the tip is added into the equation, who cares the steak was 125.00 and the pizzas are 22-27 in Italy they'd be 9 Euros.  

That's the point, this restaurant is a metaphor for downtown NYC, monied beyond repair, still kind of cool, but way more douchy then it used to be.

Fun place for a girls dinner (you can make reservations on Resy). We were seated in one of the comfy booths and ordered a medley of apps, pizzas and pasta. The 'za (we got the diavola and clam) was tasty but nothing I'd especially come back for. The tajarin with corn was awesome - like an adult mac and cheese. The broccoli rabe was also a surprise winner (though I love me any wood-fired veggies).

They don't serve cocktails, but the wine list is solid, and the waiter was good at walking us through some of the more affordable bottles (in the $55-80 range) of whites and rose. 

Hmm, what else? There's just one bathroom in the back (by the hot, hot oven), and service is included in the price.

The food was fine but way overpriced, especially considering that the small portions, and I'm a light eater. The selection of wines by the glass was nothing special though the waiter did offer two tastings before making my final choice. On the plus side, the staff is friendly and very responsive. This is def a touristy place, though I went to see what all the hype was about. 
No second time for me.
The food was good. The staff unnecessarily too pretentious. The tip is included in the otherwise high price so the staff doesn't really have to, you know, be nice.

Good restaurant...nothing bad to say. Service was great, my truffle pasta was good, not amazing, slightly over buttered. The heirloom tomatoes was delicious. Order the cuttlefish, broccoli rabe and any pizza.
Over rated.  Maybe if the waiters and staff cared about customers the experience would be worth the otherwise overpriced plates.

We finally made it and it was delicious! The waiter was wonderful and helped us select a great Rioja upon sitting down. For dinner we started with the "chips" ricotta and honey. Light fresh start to the meal. The leeks were delicious but the main stars were the guanicale pizza and eggplant pasta. I'm not a crust person but that crust was heaven. Wish I had the balls to take the leftovers home and dip into honey for a late night snack  great experience all around!! Highly recommended!

Ugh this place is beyond mediocre. I write this as I still sit in the restaurant. The service is unfriendly and standoffish, the food is fine, and the wine pour is underwhelming. Oh also, we arrived at 8:45 for a 9pm reservation and the unappealing hostess told us to wait outside / get a drink at a restaurant nearby and to come back at 9. What?! I'm pretty sure the hype comes from paid Infatuation writers. Just sayin.

The food at Pasquale Jones is out of this world. My wife and I split a margherita pizza and two pastas. It was the perfect amount of food. The margherita was one of my favorite Zas in the city. The Calabrian peppers are so good with the pizza. You have to like spice though, don't go recklessly peppering your Za unless you can handle the heat. Now to the pastas. First we had the hand-cut tajarin with sweet corn and truffle. It was one of the best things I've ever eaten in my life. This is a must try. They are very generous with the truffle too. We also had the frutti di mare. It was good, but nothing special. 

The food here is easily a 5, but the service at our visit was not. We were told it was an hour and a half wait for a table and decided to wait at a bar nearby where we received a text an hour and a half later that they are no longer seating anyone for dinner. We showed up a few minutes later where we noticed about 10 open tables and people just ordering their dinner. The hostess then hesitantly seated us and our waiter slammed down everything he brought to the table. When we left, there were still many other tables eating their dinner, so I'm not sure why we were treated as if we were extending the staff's night. Hopefully this was a one off thing.

Pasquale Jones is a lovely Italian Trattoria in Nolita. The food is inspired and delicious with an emphasis on wood oven pizzas and cuts of meat. 

On our visit we were met with a smile and a quick seat. The waiter was attentive and knowledgeable and after browsing the menu we decided on the braised leeks and the dry aged rib eye for 2. Additionally we chose a lovely Chianti from their seasonal wine menu which is quite extensive for a small restaurant.

The food was amazing and the service matched. And although it seemed expensive remember that the tip is built into the price.

It's a solid place.

I'm not exaggerating when I said that I had the best pasta in my life at this place.

Saw it on a celebrity's IG and has been on my list for a while. They only accept reservations thru their own website and it's almost always out. I go lucky to get a 12pm res for my bday wkd. It wasn't crowded but I think they are trying to set the casual not crowded vibe in the shop. 

Didn't love the summer white after we tasted it, it's not as crisp as a summer white wine. But the sparking was much better.

We had the sausage as app and we each tried a pasta dish. Both amazed by the taste (portion might be small for guys, and no bread before).

Beyoncé had her VMA after party the next day after our dine-in. That tells you something!

The check is tip-included, and it's not bad at all. Would def go back to try everything else!

I don't always get to review every restaurant I try, but after my experience I felt compelled to warn others.

I enjoyed Charlie bird more than enough on previous occasions and was excited to try it's follow up restaurant. Set my alarm to make a reservation on Resy for a date 2 weeks out. Was celebrating our 9th wedding anniversary. In the little comment/note section of my reservation I asked if we could have a more quieter table, mentioned that we were celebrating an anniversary, so we can enjoy our meal and each other on this one night away from the kids. We showed up for 5:45P res on a Thursday night. The maitre'd didn't even crack a smile as we approached and gave her my name. Now at that time, the place probably had about 4 tables occupied. We literally were given the table that was smack in between 2 couples. I'm not asking for VIP treatment, but why couldn't we at least have an End table. But still, I'm not a difficult person so I just made the best of it. My husband could be a hot head sometimes, so I'm trying not to make a situation out of it. 

We weren't too hungry so just ordered a clam pizza, which it seems everyone orders and clam pizzas are my husbands favorite thing. The pizza was decent, but it was almost like a creamy clam chowder dropped on a pizza dough and shoved in an oven. It was defintely not the best clam pizza we've ever had yet the most expensive and the smallest one.  I felt like it came 2 mins after we ordered, which was a little bizarre, but whatever. Who's gonna complain about food coming quickly. Also shared the pork shank which is meant for 2. The flavor was underwhelming, just a little herb and lots of fennel but it was cooked till tender. We didn't even finish it as it was not that great to eat. It oddly came with a sad little side of arugula that was dressed with a little olive oil and a lemon slice that you can squeeze. Sadly, I probably enjoyed that sad little side of arugula a little more than the pork shank. 

Sat around for a long time before anyone cared that we had not touched the remainder of the pork shank for awhile. Finally had to literally flag someone down to take it away. That's the thing, nobody really checks on you to see how you're doing, how the food is. The only time someone sort of voluntarily checked on us was when they wanted to see if I "cared to have another glass of wine" Go figure. We still decided to have that stupid dessert (the only choice). It seemed like a tiny bowl of reduced blueberries, topped with a Bourbon ice cream (that tasted like regular vanilla) and 4 pieces of caramel popcorn. It was the biggest afterthought of a dessert from a overhyped restaurant that I ever did see. Also was something we didn't enjoy enough to finish. At some point, someone slapped a check on our table and that was our cue that we were done. $150 for all that great experience. Worth every penny. 

Overall, I give 2 stars for a great location (to find other food if you leave feeling hungry or dissatisfied). But in terms of service, there is none. Food is subpar. We came excited for good food, fun environment, celebrating an important day and left feeling like we wasted our precious night away. I guess when people aren't working for their gratuities anymore, they just don't care. I never minded a gratuity model if the service was there, but this was utter BS. Some ppl really make a conscious effort to come try your restaurant trying to get reservations weeks in advance. Treat your customers with some integrity. My husband owns his own restaurant so he's extra attentive to the workings of a restaurant, and this kind of service is exactly what we train our staff to not do.

Great food and even better service. I must give a shout out to Daniel, one of the somms as he was so incredibly helpful on every visit, and honest as well. Being that Pasquale Jones is the sister restaurant of Charlie Bird, they did not disappoint with wine selection, stemware, and price range. I really like the small selection of half bottles - an excellent way to try new things. So I rank this experience as top of the list if you are fan of the juice - and don't be afraid to ask the staff for navigation/suggestions. Oh and the food was spot on - get the braised leeks, you would think it was pasta.

The clam pizza is out of the world! Make a reservation ahead of time to avoid the wait. Be sure to try the housemade pasta as well. One app, one pizza, and one pasta dish were plenty for two people to share. We really enjoyed our meal here on a hot summer night in August. 

The wine is definitely over-priced, but you are paying for the name and location. Just plan on going out for a drink after this meal!
Pasta and pizza are awesome. The little clam pizza was great. Super thin pizza. Not that heavy and delicious.

This place is awesome. Good food, good drinks and good vibes - all of this for your enjoyment provided you are able to get snag a reservation or are willing to wait a while for a table, even if it's 10 pm on a Wednesday night. 

When I was here, I ordered the pane carasau and shared a pork shank for two. The pane carasau is in fact not a bread course but a thin, crispy cracker served with ricotta, black pepper and honey. The ricotta and honey mixed together is delicious but the thin, brittle carasau may not be the best vehicle for eating it. Give me a loaf of thick fluffy bread, and this course would have been perfect. Highlight of the night was definitely the pork shank, which is roasted to a crisp on the outside and falling-off-the-bone tender on the inside. The best part though may be the gravy of its own juices that it's sitting in. I would cut a couple pieces of pork, take some roasted fennel and spoon gravy all over - mmm perfetto!

They have a pretty extensive wine list here with price points that should suit a wide range of budgets. The bottle of Langhe nebbiolo we had was very drinkable and paired well with our food. The waiters also seem pretty knowledgeable about the wine list so if you have any questions, just ask!

Also, I'm a huge fan of their no tipping policy. I'm seeing this more and more in NY restaurants (big thanks to Danny Meyer) and hoping more will follow.

This review is based on my first impression of the restaurant. Rude hostess!!! We walked in with no reservation and she could've been nice about telling us the time of wait but instead was rude and said 30 minutes isn't long at all.. When I fact we waited for over an hour. Good luck with building a clientele at this new spot with a rude hostess!

LOVE THIS PLACE!!!!!!

They have insanely good pasta, but their little neck clam pizza is definitely something you'll never get anywhere else.

The vibes here are awesome! They don't take reservations, but they are very good at sending you a text to let you know your table is going to be ready. 

ALSO - their wine list is amazing!!!!! They sell many of them by the HALF bottle, which is an incredible deal! (P.S. There's nothing better than drinking wine out of their glasses! They're gorgeous!!!!)

CHECK OUT MY VIDEO REVIEW OF MY TOP FOUR PLACES TO GET PIZZA IN NEW YORK: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9pPbJTKM1jQ

We went for the special San Gennaro Feast menu and they opened more reservation for this event, we luckily got a spot for two. We sat at the bar overlooking the kitchen/wood fire oven. 

- Atmosphere: very cozy, warm, and happening
- Food: very good; we had four courses meal (1st: burrata with pizza dough slices and roasted leeks; 2nd: italian mint pizza and lasagna; 3rd; beef for two roasted in the wood over; and 4th: roasted peaches topped with a special/amazing cream
- Wine list: very good in the sense that they have many reasonably priced choices and quality wines, ranging from $50 - $70; wine by the glass are also very reasonably price and good quality selections 
- Service: very nice and friendly; they were quite understanding and accommadating with us being a bit late 

Look forward to going back soon (if we can get reservation).

Great atmosphere in a fun neighborhood. The food was good; we started with the buratta (delicious; pumpkin sauce was great; bread was a bit chewey), followed by the tartufo pizza (best part of the meal) and a bowl of spaghetti (good, but lacking character). Desert of quince and vanilla gelato was excellent, especially with the toasted nuts. I will be back to try the octopus and papardele.

I had heard a lot about Pasquale Jones, there is so much hype around it. I had a friend visiting from out of town who was staying at a nearby hotel and she really wanted to try it. We decided to take our chances and walk in without a reservation on the first cold October Thursday night around 9 pm. There were empty tables but the bar was full (which is for dining only). The hostess had the typical attitude you would expect of a new trendy restaurant and said it would be at least an hour for a table, we put our names down and they said they would text/call us when a table was ready. With nowhere to stand and order a drink we walked up the street to Parm and had some wine and calamari.
Then we finished and it had now been close to 45 minutes and decided to go back, the hostess told us that she tried to call and text us multiple times (at this point we cross checked the numbers, CORRECT) but she had given our table away. Ugh, sure lol, she tried to call and text us a few times, it was almost laughable.
Anyway she says she can seat us outside, also laughable, because its like 63 degrees. Anyway she magically finds a spot for us on the side of the bar, basically next the oven. Fine, lets just eat at this point. We get the anchovy pasta, the clam pizza and the tomato burrata. The best thing we ate was the pasta, it was cooked perfectly al dente and tasted very balanced with the truffles and mild briney salty taste of the anchovies. Otherwise it was a disappointment, the tomato to burrata ratio was not on point and the clam pizza was just alright. 
Anyway, I will not be running back here, and would probably not eat here again unless I was invited to an event or group meal.

I write this with sadness in my heart. The much anticipated Pasquale Jones failed to deliver. Period. Although set in a cute and cozy space in Nolita, and after having a great experience at it's sister restaurant, Charlie Bird, I was so excited to try this spot. I had heard such great things about it and not being able to ever get a reservation, I thought there was a reason for it and it would exceed expectations. Not the case!

A relatively small space, we were seated at the bar facing an open kitchen (that's ok, it made you feel closer to the experience). We ordered the warm braised leek and walnut salad (yummy, but at $18 for barely two portions, it was a bit pricey) and the Radicchio salad (average and nothing special to write about). 

Next, we ordered the Tartufo Pizza (how it didn't even taste like truffle is beyond me) and the Wild Boar Parpadelle (barely a plate of pasta, especially for $25). These two dishes were beyond disappointing. Seriously, lacking flavor and pizzaz I can begin to describe to you how sad I was.

Finally, we ordered a roasted Quince and ice cream dessert. This I must say had to be the highlight. Drizzled with EEOV and the best sea salt, I was extremely pleased with this dessert. I guess every cloud has a silver lining? Maybe I need to give this restaurant another shot... but definitely not on my tab!

Extremely good pizza, nice atmosphere and good service BUT the prices of the beers?!?!? Hahahahah laugh is all I can do, $11-$15 for a beer... absolutely crazy!

So come here and eat, but drink water!!

The name alone has you intrigued. The impeccable service alone will certainly make you want to visit again. The staff was extremely attentive and I must say this was my 1st "no tipping" experience. 

Once my friends husbands dish arrived how badly I seriously wanted to steal his meal. He ordered the Sweet Potato tortellini which I must say was so visually appealing. Then I read the description &thought man I should've tried that. I will also go with my gut and try the Margarita upon my next visit.

Cute, quaint, intimate I throughly enjoyed the atmosphere and the tunes were such an added bonus. Lastly it was refreshing to know they were so cool to seat our friends who had to wait on us traveling from Jersey. I so look forward to our visit next month. Book your reservation now.

Tip: book a table for brunch/lunch, it's so much easier than for dinner. The huge windows also light up the room nicely during the daytime. For apps, the Speck and a salad of sunchokes, both were excellent. The speck was like prosciutto, paper-thin slices draped over sweet stewed cabbage and a tangy creamy sauce. Sunchokes are one of my favorite root vegetables, like a more earthy and sweet version of roasted potatoes, tossed with salad greens was a refreshing light appetizer. 

The little neck clam pizza was the reason we came, and it definitely delivered. It's not fishy by any means, with little jewels of juicy clam morsels sprinkled over a creamy white sauce (reminded me of artichoke pizza). Thankfully this version is on a thin crust, so it wasn't overly-heavy. The diavola pizza was also great, a nice kick of spice and a refreshing interesting touch of mint, and the mushroom and brussels sprouts pizza was a cool combo. The pizzas are the way to go here. 

The menu isn't brunchy, so it's perfect when you've really outbrunched yourself (aka you really can't look another eggs benedict in the eye). We ordered 2 apps and 3 pizzas for 5ppl, which made for a light lunch. The staff is friendly, but we ran into some awkwardness about clearing plates (as in, please don't take away our appetizer that we clearly haven't finished yet). Otherwise, a really good thin-crust pizza spot and don't miss out on that clam pizza!

I must say their clam pizza is the best. 
Now on another note. Hats off to Chef TC. We were enjoying our dinner at the stools by the ovens. And couldn't help but notice the pride he takes on his dishes. Nothing goes out without his approval. Although we haven't had the pleasure to try another dish. (Be mindful we love the clam pizza.)

They also have a very nice wine selection. Their service is always nice and welcoming.

Now, I will have to update this review once I come back and try another dish. But from past experiences this is an excellent place to impress a loved one.

Pretty cool, walked in on a cold night and got a table -- though it initially seemed like it might be a burden, even though their reservation hadn't shown. Dishes are a bit light for the price, but tasty. I'd stick with the pizza if you want more bang for your buck, just make sure they cut it before you try to eat it. We had to send it back to get cut. Not enough vegetarian either, but the food itself is solid and the atmosphere is great.
Had a delicious meal here with impeccable service. The clam pizza was great and the wine selection was impressive.

Came here with my parents to grab a late bite to eat for dinner after hearing so many great things about this place. And when I say late--I mean, we were seated around 11pm, and the place was still packed.

We were pretty hungry, so we decided to split a couple of dishes:

Braised leeks (3.5 stars): These had good flavor, but were not as tender as I was hoping.

Broccoli rabe (2.5 stars): I love broccoli rabe, but this version was a bit uninspired.

Pappardelle (3.5 stars): This dish actually had some good flavor, it was just a bit small especially considering the $24 price tag.

Margherita pizza and tartufo pizza (3 stars): I don't understand what all the pizza hype is about this place. While some of the flavors were good, I felt like they were both extremely underwhelming, especially since they are $50+ combined.

Overall, the service here seemed a bit pretentious and the food did not live up to the hype. In addition, it all seemed a bit overpriced and cramped for my liking.

Two stops here so far, and while I really enjoyed it both times, I haven't been quite as blown away as I expected, given all the hype.

The first time in, we got the margherita, agnolotti, roman gnocchi, and pappardelle with lamb ragu. We didn't love the gnocchi but everything else was very good.

The second time, we went pizza-heavy -- we got the margherita, diavola, and little neck clam, the last of which was our favorite. (The other two were very good as well, but they didn't stand out from many of the great pizza places in the city which have awesome margherita and spicy ~pepperoni-ish pies.) We also got the leaks, brussel sprouts, and carrot as sides (which we liked in that order).

Points for an ever-changing menu, and it's important to note that their menu is hospitality-included, so it's not as expensive as it looks. But I'm still waiting to really have a moment here.

Great atmosphere and service. We walked in on a week night without a reservation, luckily they were able to seat us at the bar which I actually recommend if there are only 2 people in your party.

Pros:
Familiar Italian fare with some flare
Gratuity is included
Accepts American Express
Killer decor
Incredible service, friendly staff, wonderful menu items. Dinner at Pasquale Jones was an overall great experience aside from the difficulty in securing a reservation.

I was a bit hesitant about trying Pasquale Jones, since I'd felt it'd be overrated like many of the new trendy restaurants in NY.  A couple of friends (who love Charlie Bird but haven't been to Pasquale) suggested it for lunch this past Saturday, so we gave it a go.  Both the atmosphere, the food, and the service were really nothing special.  The BF & I shared the chopped salad with salami, olive & provolone (tasty but definitely not unique) and the Little Neck Clam pizza (so over priced at $27).  Our waiter would also bump into someone at the table every time he reached over to clear our plates...

In any case, Pasquale Jones was exactly what I thought it'd be ... overrated and overpriced.

Haven't been yet. I have a reservation for dinner. I heard they have good food but not sure, should know tomorrow after I eat there, I have a reservation tomorrow night. Not sure what I will order for food, prob will see what's on the menu first. But I'll order some negronies

Hands down best clam pizza ( well it was the first time I'd ever had clam pizza so that may have been a little unfair)

Reception and being seated was seamless which I always appreciate. The waiter wasn't the warmest but that didn't stop me from enjoying the meal. We had the clam pizza and pork shank for two which I highly recommend!

Pasquale Jones is a cute and trendy restaurant that's definitely worth a try. We came in with a group of 7 without reservation and the hostess was gracious enough to help move around some reservations to fit our group in a table. Our group had a very late lunch and decided to split a lot of different menu items. 

Brussels Sprouts: Very simple dish that was well seasoned and cooked just right to leave enough crunch. Had a heap of prosciutto that provided great saltiness to the sprouts.
Little Neck Clam Pizza: Great clam pizza that reminded me of a white pizza. The small pieces of clam, coupled with a bit of lemon juice was delicious and flavorful.
Diavola: The tiny bit of mint was a great addition that complimented the salami well. 
Mezze Rigatoni: Pasta was cooked really well, but the star was definitely the sauce! It was not too watered down or too oily and contained ground pork that was very savory. 

Overall the food and service was great! I'll return to try a couple of their pastas.

Great, no-fuss versatile restaurant. Nice enough for a date or special occasion, but also great for a casual catch-up with friends.

The food is simple, in the best way possible.  The clam pizza of course is amazing- lots of places in NY do clam pizzas, but this is definitely one of the best.  The brininess of the clam is prominent, yet perfectly balanced with the touch of cream and lightness of lemon.  The ricotta appetizer is soo good, I could eat 5 of them by myself.  For entrees, my husband and I split the pork shank.  It was very flavorful, if a little salty, and on the verge of being too rich; however, they serve it with a side of arugula salad, which serves as the perfect complement to cleanse the palate and lighten things up.  The meat is fall-apart tender, although I do wish the skin were slightly crispier.

Service is on point, and they have a great wine list.  Speaking of which, they serve wine in Zalto glasses, which are just the most stunning glasses I've ever seen.  It's not something I usually pay attention to, but the second we sat down, I couldn't help but notice the gorgeous glasses (and of course flipped them over and examined them to try to figure out what brand they were).  Funny enough, a group sat down next to us and the first thing they commented on was the glasses too, and then I later read the Eater review, of which the entire first paragraph is dedicated to their Zalto glasses - so apparently I'm not the only one who was impressed.

Other things to love: tip included!  Which actually makes their prices very reasonable, and the kind of restaurant you could go to fairly regularly.  Unpretentious food done beautifully, great ambiance (intimate, but not so small you feel claustrophobic), attentive service.

Our server Antonio was BEYOND amazing and made our experience worthwhile. His recommendations were on point and didn't disappoint. 
His energy was great, and even on a busy night during a prime dinner hour he made time to chit chat with us and other patrons. Something you don't see. 

The food was amazing. And the wine that was suggested by the sommelier who was very helpful. 

So happy this new spot has come to the neighborhood. Since we love Charlie Bird.

My husband and I walked in for dinner around 10pm last night and were seated within 15-ish minutes. Honestly came for the Zalto wine glasses, stayed for the service. The wine bottle list is impressive, but there's only about 10 wines by the glass (sparkling, red, and white combined). Don't get me wrong, they're tasty choices, but if you don't want a whole bottle you may be left wanting. 

The food was on point. We both had pasta that was perfect, and light. Imagine you can't go wrong with anything on the menu. You'll leave satisfied more than full, but in a world where American-Italian food has become synonymous with massive plates of heavy food, I appreciated the delicacy.

The immediate sticker shock wears off a little knowing that service is included. And the service certainly doesn't suffer, everyone we interacted with seem genuinely kind. 

The prices are a little too high to be a regular (for me anyway), but I'll be back for low-key special dinners.

Pricey as fuck, but you knew that before you came here. 

MUST HAVES: 
clam pizza- best I've ever had. Add the chili oil. If I lived nearby I'd go broke eating this everyday. 

Pork shank- perfect exterior texture and flavor. The jus is no joke. If I was dining solo I would've drank that shit. I shamelessly gnawed on the bone. 

Dessert- whatever fruit they're roasting the fuck out of. In my case it was plums, and they were glorious. It came with mascarpone ice cream I think. 


YOU CAN SKIP:

burrata with kumquats- it was interesting and I've never had anything like it, but more interesting than tasty to be sure. I'd rather fill the table with more pizza. 

Rigatoni- you shouldn't try to split it more than two ways as it's a small portion. It's tasty enough but for the price point tasty enough won't cut it. After you've had the items above you might agree.

Went here for a friend's birthday - specifically for the Littleneck Clam pizza which was, indeed, delicious. We also had the Diavola, Spanish Octopus and Margherita. In that experience, I'd say that the more unusual the pizza, the better it was. The Diavola was spicy-tasty, not oppressively hot (there are lovely peppers to add, if you need an eye-water), the Spanish Octopus had a range of interesting, rich flavors of tomato and basil included with the perfectly cooked octopus, and the Margherita's sauce was exactly as it should be. The Littleneck Clam pizza was definitely our favorite but they really all were quite good.

The space is indeed small, and has a rather chic closeness, being dark and nookish. It's a strange but not unpleasant marriage of hip with more homey-like food. The biggest issue I had was that our main waiter (the one who took our order, not the ones who delivered it) was insistent that we should share starters before the pizza to "have the best experience of the restaurant." First, this is not described at all on the restaurant's website or on the menu - there is no obvious suggestion by the owners or the chef that the restaurant is meant as a "whole" experience. It's an expensive pizza place, with expensive other things, and my expectation was that the food was going to be excellent, regardless. I don't believe I need to have leeks before pizza as a requirement to have the "best" experience. Second, this is New York City. If we want to have just pizza and wine, by golly, that's what we're going to have, thank you. It all felt rather like an up-sell that failed on his part because I just was not having it - I found his attitude unpleasant and tiresome. I don't go out to argue with the waiter.

Two visits, one 5 star, one 3 star.  Average of 4.

First visit - 5 stars -  Prime-ish time, about 8-9 pm on a Sunday of a holiday weekend.  We watched the chef at the pass from our perch at the counter looking into the open kitchen.  You could tell he cared about the food he was putting out, cleaning up plates, putting on finishing touches, or rejecting them when they didn't meet his standards even though the place was very busy.  Each dish had to be perfect.

Clam pizza was great.   Diavola was great.  Goose pasta also great.  Skipped the black truffle pizza, shame on us because it's not on the menu any longer.

Wine recommendations were hit and miss.  Enjoyed the champagne by the glass.  When I wanted something less full-bodied than a zinfandel, I ended up with a way too fruity wine.  I could have requested something else, so that's on me.

Second visit - 3 stars (maybe 3.5 if I were generous and focused only on the braised leeks) - off hour, earlier, maybe 5 pm midweek.  Different chef at the pass.  Better perch at the counter, but that was just allowed us to see the mistakes.  We tried the octopus appetizer.  I love octopus.  Cook hands up the octopus to the head chef.  Head chef looks at the dish and asks cook: "Is your grill hot enough?" Sure enough, it wasn't and he fixed it but chef let it go and served us the dish.  FYI, wasn't hot enough and octopus was tepid and kind of rubbery.  

Reordered the clam pizza  because it was so good the first time.  Uh uh.  I was eating it and trying to pinpoint what was different/off.  I realized that it was missing the creamy sauce and the clams were overcooked this time.  The sauce had probably cooked off.  Could I have said something?  Sure, but by the time we figured it out there were two pieces missing, which just seemed tacky.  Also, quality control clearly wasn't the strong suit that night. 

Braised leeks were fantastic.  Great flavor, texture.  Terrific cheesiness.

Very good food as most here have attested to. I don't need to walk through everything we ate. Service provided by the wait staff was friendly and our waiter gave a nice wine recommendation. However, they need to train their hosts/hostesses better, especially given they are a "hospitality included" restaurant.  We arrived 12 minutes late for our reservation (our fault), and the hostess made sure to remind us they needed the table back by 8pm.  Pet peeve of mine but a restaurant should never tell you how long you have at the table, and two hours for a 4 top is pretty skinny regardless. Its up to them to move the meal along if they need the table back within a certain amount of time. Unless I'm trying to order way more food than the average diner, theres not much I'm going to do to hold up the pace of service. Reminding me that I have 1 hour and 48 minutes for my meal only creates anxiety that a diner should not have when eating anywhere, let alone when spending over $100 pp.

If you are going to jump on the hospitality included bandwagon, provide service on par with the USHG restaurants, who would never tell you they "need the table back at 8".

The salads are some of the best I've ever had in the city. 
The pizza is another story. Even though we waited it for to cool down it was a big pile of mush from the crust  inward. The sauce was eh although I will give it a shout out for the hot pepper oil mixture topping . I'm sorry but this is New York and we're really spoiled. Actually the best pizza in the area is Raza in Jersey City. What can I say I'm super picky about my carbs.
Food was barely ok, way overpriced for what is it... and trust me, there is nothing Italian in there...
We love this place. Great thin crust pizza. Pasta is always cooked perfectly. The tomatoes are singing in our mouths. We even order this on Caviar! Doesn't get any better than this.

Came here last night and was SOOO looking forward to it. Unfortunately, this place did not deliver. We ordered the ricotta appetizer,  2 pizza's + the broccoli rabe. Appetizer and Diavola pizza were great. Second pizza and broccoli rabe were just mehhh - not worth the $25 for the second pizza. Service was great but with all the GREAT pizza options in NYC....we will not be returning. Not worth it.

Good pizza, everything else is just ok. Definitely completely overpriced.

Wine list is very limited as well.

Diavola pizza - good
Bread with ricotta - $12 for a tiny portion and the ricotta was too liquid
Leeks - too rich and buttery
Fish - was ok but super tiny portion for $36

Do not come here if you're hungry.

It is a disgrace to the integrity of Yelp that Pasquale Jones has 3.5 stars. 4.5 or 5, in my mind, is far more appropriate.

In typical fashion, my dad secured a hook-up here on our first visit, so we were able to get a table for 7 for my boyfriend's birthday at the last minute. If you want to go walk-in style, there are a ton of great bars in the area to wait at (One Mile House Bar, Loreley Beer Garden, Sweet & Vicious). PJs, as we veterans call it, has a great casual, laid-back feel to it that makes for a great dining experience. We had a circular booth in the back with two chairs and definitely could've fit an 8th person. I must say, I have one HUGE problem with this place that precludes me from giving it the 5-star rating it probably deserves. They spell Broccoli Rabe in that way on one part of the menu but then as Broccoli Raab on another. This sort of inconsistency, imho, should be considered the 8th deadly sin, and is certainly more of a sin than sloth.

Recommended Appetizers:

- Warm Braised Leeks ($20) with toasted walnuts & parmigiano reggiano
- White Asparagus ($22) with tarragon & fonduta
- Charcoal-Grilled Cuttlefish ($23) with snap peas, hot pepper & mint

Recommended Pizzas:

Magherita ($22) wiht san marzano tomato, mozzerella di bufala, & basil
Littleneck Clam* ($28) with parsley, garlic, lemon, & cream

*This is basically what they're known for and is considered a can't miss

Recommended Pastas:

We went off-menu for this and had the veal/pork ragu special. Absolutely delicious

Pro Tip: Even if it's not on the menu, ask if they'll make you the calzone. It's fantastic.

I wasn't kidding when I said the spelling issue is the main thing that kept me from granting this restaurant 5 stars. Okay, I kind of was, but it did bother me, most of the table, and the waiter. If 4.5 stars was an option, that's definitely what I would've went with, but 3.5 stars is a travesty.

Went to PJ on a busy recent Friday night.  Food was excellent, wine list comprehensive, generally all around good vibe.  Two drawbacks -- for a wine-driven restaurant, the knowledge of the person helping us make a selection, was unbelievably appalling.  Seriously?
Maybe the som was off that night.  Second complaint was our waiter -- made mistakes, provided misinformation about sizing of dishes (we ordered too much), and in general, tried to up-sell us at every opportunity.  A lot of food was left on the table. An unfortunate service experience, considering the rest was excellent.

Heard so much about their pizza, but was kind of disappointed.   The salad was tasty but it I swear there was garden dirt in it as I could feel that strange crunch.  Waitress never filled our waters.  For price you pay, would not recommend.
Would have given 5 stars if the service was faster and they had gluten free pasta or pizza for lunch. Very limited but delicious options.

The service was horrible!  The attitude of the of the staff and  specifically the rude maître d' definitely has a lot to be desired.  I would never recommend this place and the silverware  was dirty.   This place was not welcoming at all and I'm sure there are plenty of other fabulous places in New York and especially Little Italy.

I live nowhere near Pasquale Jones but am still a repeat customer because I have actual dreams about the clam pizza. PQ always ends up being exactly what I want in a meal out: excellent food, polished service, a great wine list, a lively (but not overly loud) atmosphere, zalto stemware, no math. 

People who complain about it being "overpriced" are perhaps forgetting that it's gratuity included; people who complain about it being "pretentious" are adorably misguided about what it means to dine in NYC. 

The service has always been impeccable, in my opinion--attentive without being overbearing, relaxed without being sloppy (Kyle and Javier were particularly gracious at our most recent visit). The wine service in particular is stellar: the list is focused, with plenty of great pairing options and well-priced gems. When we came in recently with no res, we happily waited for our table at a nearby bar, got a text and were seated within an hour. 

Two of us shared the leeks, hamachi crudo, white asparagus, clam pizza, and the pappardelle. Every dish was thoughtfully prepared: the citrusy element in the leeks brightened the flavors and stopped the dish from seeming too heavy, the crispy bits on the crudo added a wonderful popcorn-y dimension, the white asparagus (which can so often just come across as bland and flaccid) was beautifully seasoned, the pappadelle and the clam pizza were perfection (as always). Make sure you use the addictive calabrian chili oil! 

My only complaint would be that we were seated at the bar with an unobstructed view of the gigantic, gorgeous cut of ribeye sizzling away on the charcoal grill--which caused both of us to salivate wildly and think dirty thoughts. We pretty much have no choice now but to come back and order it--challenged accepted, Pasquale Jones.

This large oven pizza spot from the creators of Charlie Bird has received a ton of hype for the pizza and it turns out to be for good reason. The crispy charred pies here are incredible with delicious dough and awesome fresh ingredients that pack a ton of flavor. Octopus from a fire grill has to be good, but it's a rare place that makes it this great. On a pie with some spicy hot chili oil it is sheer perfection. The wine list is fantastic, just like that at Charlie Bird, and perfect for sipping while seated outside beneath the awnings on a warm sunny day.
