If it weren't for the cabs buzzing by, you might briefly think you were in Europe. The fresh ingredients on the pizza, particularly the veggies really make this pizza special and worth a visit. Come for brunch and you won't have a ridiculous wait.

Pasquale Jones had been on my list for ages, but it is very difficult to get a reservation, so I was not able to try it until my most recent trip to NY. 

A friend of mine has some pull here and booked us a reservation for a party of 4. I had been dreaming of their pastas and pizzas for ages! Unfortunately, I found out the week before that I am gluten intolerant and dairy-free, so that limited what I could order. 

We shared many things including a salad, black bass, chicken, pork shank for two and an artichoke. Everything was very good and I love that they are making great use of the wood oven. The highlight for me was the pork shank. It was fork tender and had a great juicy flavor. 

When we told the waiter I was dairy free (which also includes butter) he was not the friendliest about it. It's not my choice to have these allergies, so I would have appreciated a bit more understanding. 

Otherwise we had a nice experience.

Came here for a late night snack. Wonderful pizza. Got the Margherita pizza. This is simple, but delicious. The crust is amazing. The wine list is a little pricey, but the venue is great and its right at the heart of little Italy.

The restaurant charged me $120 for canceling my reservation with less than 24 hour notice due to unforeseen circumstances and although I've tried to reach out tens of times to ask to void this charge they have not responded to my request. Will never eat there again due to this which is a shame because the food is actually good
I lived in Little Italy for 5 years and its so sad to see how the area has changed.  Pasquale Jones is mediocre.  The pizza was underwhelming.

I don't get the hype.
It's a cute spot for sure and the hostess was lovely and accommodating-- which is nice, considering it's a hip spot and they could have been intense and rude.

The duck pasta and wood fire artichoke were really disappointing.

The best thing / only good thing we ate was the clam pizza -- but honestly I still wouldn't go back, there are too many other amazing place to eat a pie (Emily) or just a slice (Joe's) or clam pizza (Pepe's).

I had one of the loveliest pasta dishes during my recent visit to Pasquale Jones.  It was a special pasta of the day so I'm not sure how useful it is for me to go on and on about this dish.  It was linguine with sunburst tomatoes, shrimp, garlic, saffron and roasted bread crumbs.  I think I actually licked my plate clean.  I really, really wanted to order another serving of this to take with me, but sadly I was visiting from out of town and all of my meals were already spoken for during the visit.  Maybe I should have ordered an extra one anyways and ate it in the middle of the night as my fourth meal.

The other food was great as well.  The white asparagus was absolutely fantastic according to my dining companion (I am not a fan of asparagus).  The only thing that was not quite a hit was the octopus pizza.  The pizza was extremely salty so only a little bit of it got eaten.  

Overall, this is a great little place.  Make sure you secure reservations as the place is not that big and fills up quickly.

If I had to compare this to Charlie Bird, I would say we had a fantastic time and the food/wine were outstanding, but if I had to pick one to return to, it's Charlie Bird hands down. Charlie Bird is much less scene-y and the initial experience there was incredibly more friendly. I also felt that the waiter upsold the food and wine a bit, which was not an experience I had at Charlie Bird.

So much hype.  The words "Pasquale Jones" entered my ear on 3 different occasions in 3 totally different social circles of mine.  

"The clam pizza is one of the best pizza dishes I've had in the city"

"Have you been to pasquale jones?"

"I hear Jay Z goes there a lot"

So As you can imagine, my expectations were high.  I tried the clam pizza.  It was so salty.  It did pair well with the light pilsner that I opted for.  The brussel sprouts.  Salty too.  I really wanted the pork shank but they ran out.  That might have been a game changer for me. I picked off my friend's dishes.  One of them had some sort of pasta.  It tasted like pasta.

went for lunch/brunch on june 24th. 
pizza crust was good (but not up to Roberta's standards). clam pizza sauce was too creamy. the pork and egg breakfast sandwich was pretty solid once i discarded the top bun and the gloppy sauce.

the real problem was the service. we were the only patrons at noon on a saturday, yet 15 mins later the snotty hostess (short hair, hatchet face) tried to seat another couple at a table right next to us. when i told her the restaurant was 90% empty, and both groups suggested a little more privacy, she only assented after rolling her eyes and saying "i'm going to have to seat it eventually". of course when we left 30 minutes later the restaurant was still empty, and there was no one at the adjoining table. some people aren't cut out for the service industry- daytime hostess might be happier in the back.

The calzone at Pasquale Jones was excellent!  Had a wonderful dinner here with a friend, and I will definitely be returning and recommending this place.  The atmosphere was quiet and elegant, service was attentive, we had great wine recommendations from our server and the food was super delicious.  Thank you, Pasquale Jones, for a great evening!
Food is decent but service is slow. Got the little neck clams pizza which was recommended as one of the most popular pizzas and the pork shanks.

Packed on a weekday night at 6pm. For appetizers, we had warm braised leeks, hamachi crudo, and broccoli di cicco - where the burrata looked like an egg and was really tasty. Little neck clam pizza was the highlight of the whole dinner - dough was thin and i like the smoked crust, clam went well with cream. For pasta, we tried Fettucine and Spaghett, and the latter was more recommended. For protein, the ribeye was medium rare and it was interesting to try the artichoke. Dessert was gelato with blackberries - just the right sweetness. Liked their bathroom as well :)
Food was good but we waited 2 hours for a table. We got a free glass of wine though. Clam pizza is a must order but pasta is just OK.

While the sauce isn't top notch, Pasquale Jones serves up an absolutely terrific pizza. The bufala mozz is great and the perfect char, complexion, and crust is spectacular. Certainly one of the best pizzas in the city.

I went here with my boyfriend on Sunday night after hearing all of the hype for a while.  Overall do I think it deserves all of the crazy hype?....not really, but I did enjoy a delicious meal and I would go back.  To split we ordered the panzanella, the clam pizza, the corn agnolotti and the pappardelle with lamb sugo. The panzanella was really fresh and yummy.  It was a good sized portion, the croutons stayed crunchy and the dressing tasted like summer (read: super yummy).   I am not a huge clam fan so I was a little weary of the pizza but I did enjoy it.  The sauce goes well with the clams and greens but is a little one-note.  It definitely benefitted from the addition of the calabrian peppers in oil they leave at the table.  The crust, while nicely charred and chewy, was too thin to hold up to the liberal dousing of creamy sauce so it became soggy in spots.  The corn agnolotti was the true winner.   It was so creamy and sweet I wish it had been bigger and I shamelessly ate all of the leftover sauce with my spoon.  Definitely one of the better pasta dishes I have ever had.  The lamb sugo on the other hand , while the homemade pasta was delicious, the lamb was tender and I loved the addition of fresh mint too the sauce, was wayyyy over-salted.  The space has a cool minimalist vibe with interesting big round leather banquet and blown-glass votives and I loved the big cement pizza ovens.  Our server and the hostess were both lovely an gave great recommendations,  They also had a great playlist and play gangster rap in the bathrooms - so win-win there.  I wish we had tried more of their vegetable dishes and would definitely recommend to others for their pasta.  This spot would be awesome for a big group where you would share lots of dishes.

Been here several times and it's delicious, trendy yet laid back with friendly and knowledgeable staff.
Hate to throw him under the bus, but our waiter Patrick was not typical of the waitstaff there.
He tried to get us to order our food almost upon sitting down, even before serving our drink order, asking a few more times when we gave no indication we were read. He did not come over once to ask about the food we'd been served, and at the end of the meal rather than asking us if we'd like dessert instead just asked if we'd like anything else, my having to ask about dessert instead.
That said, would totally go back again!

I was super excited to come here.  The atmosphere was great.  All of the service from the hostess, to the waiter, to the wine sommelier were super friendly and helpful.  They recommended a great bottle of wine from Sicily which was excellent and reasonable.  The fact that they make everything right in front of you and the kitchen is open made me really enjoy atmosphere.  Got two key bar seats right at the end in front of the main pizza oven.  The disappointing part was the pizza.  The pizza tasted great don't get me wrong, and it even had that black char on the outside which would make it looked perfectly cooked.  I ordered three pizzas the margarita, the clam & the burrata .  All the ingredients seemed top notch and they tasted great, but they have to figure out how to properly cook them.  The bottom of ALL THREE were extremely soggy and watery.  You couldn't even eat it like regular pizza without it collapsing and all of the goodness you are waiting for on top of the pizza fall down on to the plate.  I think part of the problem is that the ovens are super hot, cook the outside so quickly that it doesn't give the bottom time to cook or crisp up.  I was very disappointed in this since it's a key factor to me when having pizza, and coming from an Italian family I may have had a slice or two in my lifetime.  If they could fix this, I think this place will stay around for decades to come.

Incredible pizza (I prefer the red sauce pizzas), great atmosphere, great wine (even the glasses are spectacular). 

Really nice people too. And awesome on a summer night with the wide open bay doors. Would definitely recommend.

I feel when I am recommending a restaurant to someone I want them to experience the best thing the city has to offer for food, drinks, ambience, location that they cannot get wherever they are from.  So when I visit a city for the first time I think, what is the best thing I can get that I cannot get in NYC? Also, if there was an apocalypse tomorrow what is the best thing I can eat or drink as if it was my last day on earth?  So for NYC I do think that will have to involve the best pizza, downtown vibe that's far far away from Times Sq, and great drinks in a super secrete speakeasy after dinner.  Pasquale Jones offers all of this plus the best pizza, pasta, wine in the city. 
 Once you are in the staff is super nice and I never felt rushed or an inconvenience to them even when I was late to return when my table was ready.  The best things this place has to offer is really really awesome pizza, really great wine along with the most relaxed and nicest staff I have encountered in a trendy downtown cool setting that not too loud or too quiet so it's the perfect combination and its all the points for a first timer in the city.  Yup that really does exist in NYC believe it or not

Service was great here. Our waitress was attentive and gave great recommendations. The food was yummy, what you would expect from the area. We ordered the Diavola Pizza and Martelli spaghetti. I would've ordered the clam pizza but I let my boyfriend choose.

Visited Monday evening while visiting my Daughter. Just can't say enough good stuff about this place. Kind of in a touristy area but really had a local vibe. Top notch service, atmosphere, and food. What you'd expect from a NYC Resturant. Two great wood fired pizza's to start, a clam that tasted like the best white clam sauce you ever had, and another with red sauce and burrata cheese. Both were outstanding !! A stuffed wood fired artichoke which was the bomb, and a parpeddlle w Bolognese sause the was over the top. Put this place on your must visit list if you're in the lower East side in NYC. A great flavor of the city to be sure!!

Nice ambience however not super veg-friendly. The service wasn't the greatest - received far too much sass from our waiter than necessary. Pretty much came here after hearing Beyonce had her after party for the VMAs here so I guess I should have expected the pretentious vibe of the staff. Overpriced for the mediocre quality of food. You can definitely find better food in NYC. Wasn't horrible but wasn't worth the price- overall, unimpressed.

We enjoyed our dinner at Pasquale Jones. We started off with the octopus, salad and squash; all 3 appetizers were delicious. I had the lamb as my entree, which was ok but nothing memorable. My partner had the chicken and it was delicious. I highly recommend ordering the artichoke side as it is very flavorful. The restaurant has a great wine list. I will definitely return!

From its colorful, kitschy neon sign to the heaping bowl full of gelato at the end of our meal, this place had me at "ciao." We shared a delicious insalata--think deconstructed Caesar--crispy octopus, spicy artichoke, and some of the best pizza to churn out of a brick oven in awhile. The mains were also exceptional. My roast chicken on sweet peppers was yummy. But the highlight was a diverse wine list with a friendly, experienced sommelier to help us choose some really interesting libations. You will not be disappointed by Pasquale, so tutti alla tavola para mangiare!
Love this place - intimate, nice environment and amazing food. I suggest the clam pizza, leeks and any of the pastas. The wine is amazing too. I'll definitely be back.

They're really aggressive with confirming your reservation. Like texting you 2 days before, 1 day before, then 30 minutes before. And then when you arrive on time the table isn't ready. And still isn't ready 20 minutes after your reservation time that they confirmed with you 3 times. 

The ricotta app is tasty. Crispy rosemary flatbread, honey and black pepper on warm ricotta. The Diavola and Margherita pizzas are fine too. I don't think it's worth $25/pizza though. 

Servers are friendly and efficient. 

I'm unclear what the mega-hype is but ‍.

I stopped in with my mom for an early dinner.  The Host asked us if we'd prefer to sit inside/outside or at the bar.  We said inside because it was hot outside.  He looked around the restaurant for a table and then told us that there would be a 5 minute or so wait.  I don't know exactly how many tables they have in the dining room, however, there were 4 tables taken.  The rest of the restaurant was empty...Bar, dining tables as well as the tables outside.  We stood and waited bc we thought there was a real reason why they didn't just seat us at one of the many vacant tables.  While we waited, a party of 3 showed up and a female Hostess showed them immediately to a table.  After 5 or so minutes, the Hostess said that she could seat us and showed us to two bar seats.  We distinctly told them that we preferred to sit at a table and not at the bar.  She then stood there as if she didn't know what to do so we helped her out by walking out.  
If the restaurant had a policy for walk ins and were a "reservations only" establishment, then they could've said so when we requested a table for 2.  No one ever mentioned reservations to us.  I honestly don't understand why there was a problem seating us.  We felt so disrespected.

I love the pasta dishes here. Always unique and seasonal. The pizzas are above average. I must say, the clam pizza is pretty overrated. Was skeptical of it when I heard great things, and it was definitely a bit overrated. not huge on fish pizza, but still, not the best pizza in the city. Everything else was very good though.

Don't believe the hype  , Don't waste 3 hours of you're life you can never get back on horrible overall  experience ! 

Better of going around the corner to several established locations  for  Better pizzas and better experience   . I wish Pete wells would stop in here !  

Manager likes to chat up women and comp there checks . Front hostess gives tables to regulars . The Waiter forgot  our  order so pizza took 45 mins !! We had several apps  which had no taste ! 

Pizza is ok surprised only 5 options .  

Cons - no tipping policy so staff have no incentive to give good service .  

Pizza very average . Whoever is doing there PR IS is killing it cos I don't see anything in place to suggest it should get all the reviews !!
The pizza was okay, not great but not bad. Ordered the diovola (hot pepper) pizza. Pizza was small for what you pay. the peppers and mint did not really compliment each other as I had hoped.
Went here with my gf after a hair cut. We sat at the bar and the service was great. The pizza was delicious.
We opted for two pasta dishes and fully enjoyed our meal. The pasta was delicious and the service was great.

Birthday party with friends, had a great time. Sommelier recommended two great wines that complimented our meal very well. We had a special pasta that used to be on the menu stuffed with butternut squash which was outstanding. Server Tucker who had just moved into town a few months ago was very patient and accommodating of our loudness.  Dessert: Gelato with poached pear and cookie crumble. Delicious!

Expensive and did not live up to the hype.

I made a simple Google search "best restaurants in soho" and Pasquale Jones was ranked as a top restaurant in many blogs. Although it only had a 3.5 rating on Yelp, I decided to give it a try.

My friend and I didn't make a reservation for dinner on a Saturday, but we were able to get a spot at the bar. The restaurant seemed to be very popular given that all the tables had been reserved. But by the time we had finished our meal, about half of the tables were still unoccupied.

The food was ok. My friend and I shared a pasta and a pizza, and it was enough food for the two of us. I wished we had ordered some greens because our meal was very heavy and greasy. Given that each item was more than $20, I would've preferred something tastier and lighter.

Pasquale Jones has a coat check, which is nice. But, we had paid our check and ready to go, but we had to wait an extra 5 minutes to retrieve our items from the coat check.

-- 
taste / 3
aesthetics / 4
vibe / 4
service / 2
price for quality / 2
OVERALL / 3

My review of Pasquale Jones is 2 stars because, Meh, I *have* experienced better. I really wanted to love it. The food was tasty but the service was extremely lacking. I take issue here since this establishment is gratuity included. My group of three shared dishes and a bottle of wine.  We ordered the warm ricotta dip (very small and strangely not served in a bowl), margarita pizza (hard to mess up), pumpkin and sage ravioli (very good), roasted brussels sprouts (just okay). The ricotta dip came out right away and there was a bit of a wait for our Margarita pizza.  We completely finished the pizza, then, another identical pizza was placed before us by one of the three people staffing our tables various needs.  We debated eating the 2nd one, but it was taken away 2 minutes later by our server who gave us a puzzled look. We explained our original order again.  Our pasta dish should have come out with the first pizza, but instead, we waited around 20 minutes for it.  And then another few minutes for our side of sprouts.  With a gratuity included establishment, what am I paying for exactly? Certainly not a smooth or friendly experience. We weren't offered anything by our server during the mix-up (a complimentary beverage, an explanation, an apology!?) We had to ask in exasperation what we could expect for the rest of our order, and only then did we get a reassured, "don't worry, the pasta is coming."  Rest assured, I didn't elect to dine out to worry whether or not my food was coming...and I won't be visiting Pasquale Jones again. This was all at 7:15 on a Tuesday.  Our total bill was just over $150.00 for three.

Just add a wonderful lunch. Very short menu which screams made fresh today. Modern setting with full view of all the action.
The pasta with sea urchin and crab meat was delicious. The chef sel rejected the pizza that was supposed to be served to our son because I did not meet his standard. 
Will go back.

Lovely little spot in soho for dinner. It was my first time,that a restaurant indicates that there is no need to tip the waiter, that the tip is already included on each menu item. So that was nice!
We had a delicious pasta, with squash, it was delicious! The pizza was also very good and the octopus!
Great food, and great cool soho vibe! Went for dinner with my husband a few months ago and loved everything we tried. We had the clam pizza, a pasta with uni dish and a great salad.

You walk in, smell (and feel the warmth of) the wood fire and you feel like you're part of an exclusive club. The wine menu is unusual and extensive and the servers know their stuff. Clams are my absolute favorite thing and I haven't had a better clam pizza anywhere...believe the hype. I don't remember what else we ordered but it was all good, however the clam pie is what I'd go back for. Tip included, which makes everyone's lives easier.
If I could give zero stars I would. The service is awful. I would absolutely never go here again. Pizza is pizza and this place is not worth it.

It's not really that great. It is always packed though, so definitely make a reservation and stick to it because there's a cancellation fee. 
The clam pizza is FIVE STARS, BABY! Dang, that thing is good. However, this place is overpriced for the quality of the food and the portion sizes. I don't think I'll be going back. It does have a nice date night ambience.

Due to the fact that I ate at Charlie Bird (other affiliated property) and it was fantastic in all aspects I was eager to try Pasquale Jones. Though the food was delicious with very small portions... even the wine, the service was just uncomfortable. Our waiter was obnoxious and frankly, annoying. Our meal was rushed and we were in and out for dinner in under 55 minutes. Service is everything!

Very cool inventive menu: eclectic and fun. 

Started with the burrito toast ( ok) and the leeks, which were totally new to me and delicious and well worth it. 

Pizzas; had the diavola and the Brussels
Sprout. Both were just ok. I am
A big NYC pizza person and these don't really do it for me. Along the lines of Pauline Gees, Roberta's, just not as good. Nice doughy crust, charred but not too hard. 

Drinks were very minimal
And very pricey. 

Overall this was a very expensive pizza experience and there are way too many good NYC places to justify the cost. 

Basically $180 for 3 people for lunch is way too much in my opinion.

Omg some of the best pizza I've ever had. We wanted an authentic pizza experience while in New York, and I want to go back just to eat at this place again! We started with the ricotta cheese and honey appetizer, which was so simple but fresh and addicting! We ordered the littleneck clam pizza and burrata pizza, both of which were amazing, but the clam took the win! The crust was so thin, light, and chewy at the same time! Make sure to order some of their house peppers, not sure what they're called but they're in an oil and add a nice spice to the pizza. Highly recommend!

Dua forno - two large wood burning ovens dominate this pizza spot from the creators of Charlie Bird. PJ's has received accolades from foodies and celebrity chefs for the pizza. The crispy yet tender charred pies here are excellent with flavorful dough and bright fresh ingredients that scream local quality. In the social media lovefest about PJ's the most hyped of all the pies is the clam pizza; and I have to agree it's sublime. The preparation is minimalist in approach. The bianco style 12 inch pie is lightly studded with tender minced baby clams and flecks of broccoli rabb with a hint of red chili spice atop a briney garlic cream. Remarkable. 

That's the good news. The bad new is the price which was remarkable too at $30. Don't get me wrong, I'm willing to pay up for quality and this pizza is great, but with about $3 worth of ingredients the price seems excessive particularly for the "personal pizza" size. I could easily eat two of these as a pizza meal. Add to that $15 for a 10 ounce glass of Mo pale ale on tap (yes $15!!) and with tax you are up to $49 for a lite meal of pizza and beer. Although it was good, my marginal personal value just can't get me to feel it was worth the price.

Allowing a 5 for the pizza and a 1 for the value, I'm at a 3 overall.

The first three times I went here, I would have given it six stars if I could have, but the new menu (the website is not up to date) is less vegetarian friendly than before. We ordered a white pie, and asked to substitute the pork with a veggie, the waiter suggested broccoli, but it wasn't on the pizza. Always disappointed though, when my best option is to remove meat from something -- I know I'm not getting the best version of the dish before it even comes, and I'm still paying for the meat. And sure enough, the pizza was really meh, whereas in the past the pizzas have blown my mind.

The food was excellent and the service excellent. What more to say? It is very popular so hard to get a reservation. They don't let you sit down until all your party are present (I understand why a restaurant would do this, but I take a star off for that reason, since it isn't the most hospitable start to an evening). They have a no-tipping policy, which means the total price is actually cheaper than the menu looks (no added costs). I feel this is a more respectable way to treat staff. The staff seemed friendly, professional and well-informed about food and wine. 
The food was great all round, and the atmosphere cozy yet glamorous.
Loved the pizza and dining experience.  Reminds me of when I was in Italy (Great food and wine!)

In all fairness, my second visit was a totally different experience. While paying for the pizza bread is annoying and I don't like the wine glasses which are plastic, this food is a mirage among mediocrity.
Ate:
Pizza bread
Leeks
Chicken saltimboca
Drank: Cabernet franc
While the pizza bread is all that- charred, salty, perfection so are the cheeses, lemony leeks. My chicken saltimboca plated like a rainbow was TDF. My friend's Spanish octopus was also lovely. Well, now I can send well deserved food accolades.

Had a delicious group dinner here tonight! I always disregard any food reviews that say "doesn't live up to the hype". Why don't you review the food and service and not the "hype"?

Food breakdown:
-Fennel salad: I've had better, probably wouldn't order again and would opt for the beets, which I've heard are very good or had an eye on the cauliflower
- margarita pizza: amazing sauce, very very fresh! I tried it with some of the pepper oil they had, very good.
- mushroom pizza: the smell of this pizza was just as good as the taste. Great white pizza albeit a little salty
- hot salami pizza: delicious but I've had better (think emilys colony) 
- artichoke pasta: a perfect balance of decadent and richness with the spicy honey was a great way to end our meal
- sweet potato and lemon aioli: MUST ORDER. I have recently been turned onto sweet potato dishes and the lemon aioli is really the game changer here.
An amazing dining experience. Everything was great. The staff was very attentive and no detail was left unaddressed. Will definitely be coming back.

Booked dinner last night with clients. Not very prompt in the beginning to get the meal started and couldn't believe the rudeness upon completion.  After spending hundreds of dollars we were basically told our "time" was up and we would have to leave. Although the food is good customer service is everything and I will never go back.

Disclaimer: I am not giving this place 5 stars because we have the same first name. They have some kicka$$ pizza! 
Place is really small and we sat at the counter (I guess it's called that) with a perfect view of the pizza making. 
Their dough is so damn good but it costs a lot of dough to purchase a small (all one size) pie. $24 for one...no lie...BUT...it includes tip. Yup, they don't accept tip. The service, even though it included tip, was great. Super friendly and quick. We ordered the CHANTERELLE MUSHROOM (Mozzarella di Bufala, Arugula & Pecorino Romano). One of the best pies I have ever had...so light and the crust was delicious! I could eat that all day long. 
They serve beer (2 on tap)/wine (several to choose from glass/bottle) but no spirits. 
They close for a couple of hours between lunch/dinner. We were there when they reopened. Be advised it gets busy. Well worth waiting. 
Pasquale Approved! ENJOY!

Be prepared to wait for food, but everything else is A1. Service and food is wonderful. Ambience is top notch. Not to mention they play a great mixture of old school R&B.
Great to come with friends or on a date if you want to impress.
The pizza is superb. Came here with friends and we got our first round of drinks comped because the wait was so long. Shout out to the hostess, Alison. We tried the margherita pizza, the littleneck clam, and the artichoke pasta. Delicious across the board.
They only serve wine and beer just as an FYI.
Must try!
It was my first time trying clam pizza in nyc. It was tastier than I imagined (: not sure if portions were for sharing.. I finished a pie on my own :D

I liked my experience here. From what I ordered the pea shoot pizza stood out the most. I found the flavors really unique, the tastes paired nicely with each other but they stood out on their own as well. The pizza was perfectly charred and perfect texture. The menu changes a lot here, which is a plus or minus for some.
I had dinner at the bar, which I don't prefer, I find it claustrophobic , but it was ok once the neighboring diners moved over a bit. It also meant no wait which was a plus. The workers seem jolly and happy and while I didn't interact with them much it was nice to see a happy work place. The bathrooms and the space are very very clean. 

In short, dinner was great, no wait, happy staff. (Also the infatuation says the pizza here gets an A+ and you can't argue with them). One star off because of price, it was a steep bill for the little ordered.
best food i have ever had in my life 15/10 everything was beyond amazing definitely recommend

Went here for a birthday dinner and there was a private event so they told us to come back at 7 pm
to seat us (had also spoken to someone on the phone weeks prior.) They said (in a not full restaurant) they could place us inside for only an hour dining time and had to be out within the hour  or outside in the cold where the whole party would not be able to sit. A person had to leave the birthday dinner in order for the group to sit, everyone shivering outside (waiters did not even make a hint of apology), rushed us through our orders and brought out multiple birthday desserts (without asking if we wanted more than 1) and charged us for all the desserts. Inconsiderate and disrespectful wait staff. Unfortunate that they didn't seem to care at all if they were ruining our experience.

Friday night out with some friends and Pasquale Jones was our dinner spot. We called a week in advance to make a reservation, so make sure you do that! We were seated slightly after our reservation time but all good on that.
The menu is pretty small so expecting big things! At first glance everything looks a bit pricey for pizza and pasta, but there is a note at the bottom of the menu noting this is a non-tipping restaurant, so price you see is what you get. My first non-tipping restaurant, yay!
For 3 of us we proceeded to order a bottle of wine for the table, the Ricotta toast app, the leafy green salad, Diavola pizza and 2 pasta dishes one veg and one meat.
The Ricotta was served with a really thin crispy toast, and Ricotta was good (when is it not?) but I wish the bread was different. The salad was a simple salad- pretty good clean way to start the meal.
The Diavola pizza came out next and although I know Diavola is generally spicy, this had a real kick and I was struggling a bit. The pizza here has a really nice thin crust, I think I just would have been happier with another set of toppings.. 
Our 2 pastas came out last, both were little ravioli dumpling like- one filled with artichoke and the other the Suckling Pig. Both were good but the general consensus was the Artichoke was better! 
Portions were not large (and I wish we got more food for the price) so we had room for the house dessert, they only offer one. A rhubarb cobbler of sorts- pretty delicious first couple bits until I realized there were nuts in it and I'm allergic!
General thought is that it was a good but expensive meal, nice atmosphere but not a standout, and I likely would not jump to go back.

This place has been on my list forEVER and I'm so glad I finally made it in! Being on infatuations list of top pizza places in NYC also helps.

I came with a friend and we ordered two pizzas - the classic margarita (the best way of telling if a pizza place knows what they're doing) which was 10/10. The crust was cooked to perfection, great sauce to cheese ratio.

We got adventurous and also tried the little neck clam pizza largely due to its well deserved popularity on yelp. This was surprisingly delicious and gave the margarita pizza a run for its money, also 10/10. The clams were so fresh, served with a lemon on top to squeeze on the pizza, and all of the flavors complemented each other to perfection.

The staff was nice and attentive, was happy to offer recommendations on food and wine.

Absolutely fantastic pizza spot, I can't wait to return!

I love this place!! Our server Lauren was all smiling and very happy to help. Love the fine glass wares of this restaurant. They are all by Zalto. Very pretty! Their mushroom pasta was very tasty, and their pork shanks were cooked to perfection. The best thing I love about this place is the waitstaff. Another thing I like about this restaurant is tips is included in the bill. Maybe that's why the price of the dishes are a little high, but I'm totally ok with it, coz the service is great and the food is great!

Quite possibly the best meal we've ever had!   My husband and I sat at he counter - a treat to watch the chefs at work.  I recommend sharing dishes, so as to enjoy all the amazing flavors.  We shared calamari with spring peas and mint, a special white pizza and a sweet corn cappelletti.  Wood fired pizza crust is light and tasty. Pasta is melt in your mouth.  All delectable and beautifully presented. Service was excellent, everyone very friendly.   Thought prices were reasonable for NYC. Can't wait to go back.

This place was on my list of dinner places in NYC.... that was IF I could get a reservation. It is pretty hard to get a reservation here unless its a week or two out. A week out, I was only able to get the earliest reservation of the evening for a table for two. 
We arrived and sat down at the table and ordered some wine while we reviewed the menu. I was surprised at how small the menu was and did not see very many vegetarian options (yikes!) 
We ordered a pizza to share since we were starving, we went basic with the Margherita. For my entree, I knew I wanted a pasta dish, but all of the dishes had meat. I asked the waiter about a meatless pasta dish, he was extremely accommodating and was able to put an order in for a meatless pasta dish with no hesitation. 
All of the food arrived at once, the pizza, and a beautiful dish of Cacio e Pepe. The food did not disappoint! It was really delicious! The only downside was that the food came out super fast and the waiter kept visiting our table asking if we needed anything and were ready for the check. We did want to enjoy another glass of wine but felt like they were trying to push us out to prepare the table for the next reservation. We decided to pay and move onto another location for more wine.

A top nyc pizza contender! Both the food and service, especially the bus boys, were great. We ordered the ricotta, burrata pizza and the pork agnolotti.

The ricotta was rich, creamy and well seasoned. It came with some flatbread and honey which were great accompaniments. 

The next course was the pizza, and wow! Amazing crust, super flavorful sauce, burrata and anchovies add up to a perfectly balanced pizza that was just delicious. I think the tomatoes were the best tomatoes I've had outside of Italy. 

After, we had the agnolotti. The pasta color was beautiful and had a great thin texture. Unfortunately, the filling and brown butter sauce were a little one note. While tasty, it was my least favorite part of the meal. 

I cant wait to return and try more pizzas!!

Come for the pizza, stay for the pasta (and the wine! Side note: to the Yelper who claimed that the wine glasses are plastic: WTF, not only are they glass, but they're Zalto, every wine enthusiast's fave!)

Pasquale Jones is a gem, especially considering the surrounding neighborhood, which is saturated with mediocre Italian restaurants. PJ's better than the much-hyped Rubirosa and to be honest, I think it's better than Charlie Bird. I know, I know, controversial opinion! 

We've never had a bad dish, but our favorites include the Japanese cucumber salad, clam and diavola pizzas, and agnolotti. 

Crucially, the ambiance is just right: the ideal combo of upscale and relaxed, appropriate for millennials and grandparents alike. While it can be tricky to get a reservation (I remember trying endlessly when they first opened), just try walking in! My husband and I have successfully walked in without a wait countless times. What are you waiting for, go!

Me and my friend were here for lunch, we ordered one clam pizza, one chicken alla romana, and one arugula for starter. The clam pizza was amazing, I myself am mostly not that into pizza, but the clam pizza they have had such a rich and also delicate taste, I would highly recommend it. Chicken alla romana was just ok, not bad but not as good as I expected.
1.5 hour delivery time, arrived cold. $35 dollars for 19 noodles. Oh and they forgot the meat. Enough said

This place was surprisingly empty for lunch. Not sure why since I had heard it is pretty good. We came anyway.

The lunch menu isnt too expansive and even with not many options for lunch they didnt have one of the options (the berkshire pork milanese). Just an fyi... this is a Non-tipping establishment which is very interesting. I guess they factor it into the bill.

I ordered the frittata which was pretty good. The eggs were fluffy and the seasoning was on point.  My guest said the pasta was al dente and not over-sauced. 

I hear the brunch is better so maybe if I am in the area I will come back for that. I probably wouldn't go out of my way to come back.

my wife and i recently visited for a early dinner
food looked and smelled delicious , service good
food tasted great , unfortunately my pork filled pasta dish would'nt fill a five year olds belly. terrible portions...
oh , and the 15 dollars for a  glass of beer  , come on
we most definitely won't return
My favorite pizza and pasta place in SoHo. I always go and love it. The Burrata is also a great choice.

Beautiful and small place with very very good execution on everything.

Maybe the size has to do with why it's so hard to get a resy.

Pizza is really good. Had the Clam Pie.
Tagliatelle with Lamb was solid.
Rhubarb and Strawberry bake with gelato was very good.

This is great pizza. As good as any you will have, depending on your style preferences it will be near the top of your list. I was lucky enough to grab a solo seat at the bar/kitchen seats. Service was fast as my pizza came within 5 minutes of placing my order. The Diavalo was fantastic...mint was a nice touch that I haven't had on pizza before. I'll have to come back to try some other items on the menu. Only knock I would note is that the wines by the glass list was short...maybe 10. Id expect a more lengthy list at pizza/Italian place known for its wines.

Had a delicious pizza while enjoying the view at the bar. We got to see how our pizzas were made and it was some great entertainment! Definitely recommend this place to anyone who wants to try the best pizza in New York!

Good food but way toooo many rules.  Can't put ice in wine glasses bc they said they will break.  Wouldn't allow us to enter restaurant until exact time of reservation bc it was for the same exact time as opening. A lot of little weird things however the food was delicious.

I seldom venture downtown unless absolutely necessary but I had heard great things about this place so I went on a week night for dinner with friends and left feeling pretty good!

Decor: super adorable and warm atmosphere. Crowd is mostly young professionals, dates, friends, a few coworkers maybe. No tourists, thank goodness.

Food: calamari appetizer, totally average. Clam pizza was decent.. and the spicy pepperoni with mint on their specials menu was quite amazing. Plus the chili oil on the side all made it delicious.
We also shared the truffle pasta from the specials menu as well as the mortadella but it was a bit salty.

The pepperoni pizza was memorable as was the truffle pasta but I wouldnt say it was spectacular. 

Service was OKAY. Food took forever to arrive and the service was inconsistent but I suppose the waitstaff there is very lean. 

Checked this place off my nyc bucket list!
I would try exploring other places next but if you are in the area, why not stop by here and give it a go? :)

Ah, also, price and portions.. $$$$$$

There is no denying that their appetizers and pizza are exceptional, and I was fairly impressed with this place the first few times we visited.  That being said, the prices are ridic.  For some reason, I can forgive the prices for the pizza, but when I ventured off course recently and tried a pasta...  the portion was beyond insulting, like some kind of a joke.  And it's not like the few bites I got to eat were even anything so delicious (not even in the same league as Scarpetta).  To add insult to injury, they were "out of" their "signature" leek appetizer, and it was 6:00 on a Saturday!  Shout out, though, to host Ashley.  She is a doll -- so warm and friendly and does her best to accommodate. I don't get how she doesn't lose her patience with all the walk-ins!

Awesome. It's expensive but really worth it if you truly love a mind blowing pasta dish and pizza. We spent over 100$ on a small pizza, and two pastas but it was so worth it. Best pasta I've ever had. Insane pizza. Small portions but again it's about the quality- and this quality is unreal.

Come at lunch. Pasta was excellent. Pizza was quite good. The vibe and crowd was upscale yet easy going. Bright, clean space, somehow ever-so-slightly homey. Not a huge lunch crowd so it's easy to start depthful convos. Their menu has changed slightly since I've been, but the flavors are confident and contextualized.

Not a bad pizza, but you can get better without trying too hard.  The focus here is being a "trendy" place vs. solid food and service

Food: 5/10
The pizza was decent, but you can get comparable pizza at a lot of other places

Service: 3/10
Below average service for a proper restaurant.  They didn't change our plates out between the salad and pizza (added a vinegar taste) and then proceeded to pull away plates and utensils before we finished eating

Decor: 4/10
OK decor, nothing special, but looked presentable.  The bar area makes no sense as the wait staff constantly bumps into the diners and then reaches across your face for everything they do

Price: $40 per person (assumes shared pizza, shared small app, 1 drink, tax, and tip.)  Not terrible, but better value elsewhere

Overall: 4/10
If you have to go here it's fine, but find another place if you can

I truly can say having been eating out in some of the very best Italian restaurants in NYC and the five boroughs, Pasquale Jones did not live up to the reviews at all. Im not sure if the people that eat there really know good pizza and really good Italian food. I was truly disappointed with all of it. The arugula salad had no dressing at all , the broccoli rabe claims to have garlic and it was absolutely tasteless, the skate had no flavor thank god for a few capers and the pizza dough did not have enough salt in it, I asked for mushrooms on the margarita pizza and they had mushroom shavings on it... no taste. Finally the so called signature clam pizza was canned clams and soggy. I hope Im not being mean but you need to bring it up more then a notch. I have eaten in Mezzagiorno, Bar Pitti, Lucali Pizza, the list can go on and on... not even close

The only bad thing about this restaurant is how hard it is to get a reservation before 10pm. The pizza has never once disappointed me (try the clam!) and the service is really good, especially considering this is a restaurant where gratuity is already included in the price.

My wife and I had an amazing dinner at this restaurant! The atmosphere was comfortable and the playlist was on point. The staff was super friendly and sensitive to all of our needs. All in all this is one of the best date nights we have ever had and I would recommend this place to all

If you're lucky enough to get a reservation at this coveted pizza joint, then put on your stretchy pants because you're in for a great night. And if you're not so lucky (like me), then stop in early, put your name down, and head to a neighboring bar to pass the time as you wait for a table. Trust me, this place is worth the wait. 

We started with the RADICCHIO salad, trying to get a little greenery in before we gorged on pizza and pasta. The radicchio is crunchy, and pairs well with the sweetness of the pear and pecan, as well as the pungent gorgonzola drizzle. 

It was hard to decide between the many delicious-looking pizzas, but we settled on the MORTADELLA. The crust is thin and crispy, with those burnt bubbly edges you love to pick at. The pizza has a white base, and is covered entirely with thin slices of mortadella straight from the deli, all topped with a balsamic drizzle. When we ordered this, we were expecting the mortadella to be crispy and baked onto the pizza, but we cannot fault the restaurant for our own expectations. The pizza was still delicious!

We complimented the pizza with the divine PUMPKIN CAPPELLACCI. The cappellacci are big pasta dumplings, with a sweet and savory pumpkin filling, and bathing in a luscious sage and brown butter sauce that is simply scrumptious. The portion wasn't overwhelmingly big, which was good since we just devoured an entire pizza. I highly recommend this pasta!

Definitely make a reservation in advance, and if not, expect to wait. This place is packed, and for good reason. The food here is very delicious!

B+ for ambiance/vibe
B for food
D for service

Another NYC hotspot with good (but not great) food, decent enough vibe/ambiance, and utterly disappointing service. 

As 2 couples in our late 20s, we were looking for a good/fun restaurant to celebrate our engagement. For a couple weeks leading up to our reservation, we were calling the restaurant to find out of they had a full bar. Unfortunately, the phone just rings and rings and nobody ever picks up. Upon arrival, we were disappointed to learn that they in fact did not have a full bar (just wine and beer). By simply picking up the phone or having a way to communicate, we could have learned this prior to arrival. We asked the maitre d why they don't answer their phone, and he rudely responded "We've been here for 3 years now so I think not answering our phone is working just fine for us." A more snobby response there is not. This guy might as well have been wearing a sign on his shirt that said "Because we're a hot restaurant, I have no interest in being kind or demonstrating customer-first service, so don't expect it."

I've worked in hospitality for the last 10 years and have dined at the finest restaurants in the city to the most hole in the wall. From 11 Mad Park to your local dive, the fact remains, is that service will always be king, and the restaurants that are fooled into thinking they do not need to put service first, will ultimately not last. This guy was smug as could be (if anybody is interested in identifying him, he had brown hair, parted hair, beard, mid 30s), and we sat at our table already having a pretty bad taste in our mouth.

From there, our waiter tried to help us through selecting a wine. He was not a bad guy, but he pushed us towards a wine from Piedmont and after trying the wine and not really loving how light it was, he tried convincing us that the Nebbiolo grape is in fact a "light" grape. As a wine collector and fairly knowledgeable wine drinker, this simply is not correct -- the Nebbiolo is notorious for being one of the biggest, boldest and most tannic grapes in the world. We respectfully disagreed at which point he self-proclaimed himself the "sommelier," at which point we decided to let it slide and drank our uninspiring $100 bottle of wine.

From there, no real complaints. The food was pretty good but nothing to write home about it. Clam pizza was definitely the standout and the only thing that was unique or interesting. The other pizzas and pastas you could find at 100 other pizza/pasta joints in the city. 

And given the uniformity of their food, you would think they'd really try to focus on their service. Sadly, this was not the case, and we left feeling we had a meal that was decent at best, with a bottle of wine we did not enjoy and service that all but said "F you, we are not interested in the quality of your experience."

Sad to see more and more restaurants go this direction. The good news, there are still hundreds of restaurants out there that honor an old school approach of focusing on quality of service and experience. Sadly, this is not one of them.

$26 for a pizza that my friend said was "ok". $12 for fifty cents worth of salad greens because they had nothing else I could eat. And the worst service a restaurant could offer. Why do people eat here?

Two words for this place ... So Good !! 
My friend and I came here on Dec 29. We had a 930pm reservation and showed up a bit early , to accommodate for the wait they gave us complimentary glasses of Prosecco ! 
We were seated at the bar type area so we had a great view of the food prep and wood burning stoves . 
We ordered the Margarita pizza , the crust was so soft and the mozzarella was amazing . They served it w/ a spicy oil which was super spicy and added that extra kick !  I ordered the tagliatelle special of the night w/pork meat sauce, the pasta was cooked perfectly and the meat sauce was seasoned just right !

We ordered a bottle of white wine but soon realized that we did too much day drinking and would not finish the bottle . Our waiter was kind enough to box it up for us so we could take it to go ! 

Although the menu is very minimal the options they have are tasty and reasonably priced . I will definitely be coming back and bringing more friends to experience this gem!

happy i was finally able to try this joint as i dont get out of the house a lot this days (self diagnosed seasonal affective disorder effects 99/100 new yorkers). upon entry, i was immediately taken by the badass decor. absolutely loved the steeze. very dark, modern, open kitchen, nice booths. tried a lot of the fare and was impressed by the pasta and gelato. gonna keep it real: you can get way better pizza than here. but hey thats okay! pasquale jones has it going on otherwise, including great service, so its worth a visit. fyi - beer and wine ONLY and the wine list leaves something to be desired considering the prices are upwards of $50/bottle. good spot for a small group gathering.

There is a reason why this place is nearly impossible to get into. However, if you're willing to go at odd times or book on resy in advance, you shouldn't have difficulty getting in. We chose to come at 3pm on a Sunday and made our reservations the same day. Four of us went and each ordered our own pizza. I would suggest doing the same as they are the size of personal pizzas. 

We ordered the following:
-Margherita Pizza (we ordered two of these): 4/5 It was a great pizza option, but it was not terribly exciting for me. 
-Littleneck Clam Pizza: 5/5 I heard great things about this pizza, so I chose to try it even though I had reservations about seafood on pizza. So glad I did! I try to eat on the healthy side, and this was perfectly light. 
-Pizza Diavola: 5/5 This was amazing as well- like your traditional pepperoni spicy pizza. This one was on the heavier size and is the only dish that wasn't finished because of how heavy it was with the meat. 

My favorite part though was the crust. It wasn't too thick but was still perfectly soft.

My only complaint (and reason why we didn't give 5 stars) was the service. It was difficult to figure out who our server was, and we were without water a few times. At one point, I rationed how much water I would allow myself to drink because I didn't know when it would be filled. We also asked the server for parmesan for the pizza, and he never came back with it. He never remembered, apologized, or checked in on it. By the time we were able to find him again, we had already finished the pizza.

Pasquale Jones serves some of the best pizza in NYC. If you enjoy doughy pizza crust, you will love this place!! The crust is still thin enough to be considered "healthy" and in doing so, elevates the toppings which are amazing and flavorful. 

The Littleneck Clam pizza is a MUST TRY!! It's the best one on the menu and maybe even in NYC. The taste/saltiness of the clams are not too overwhelming. The Diavola pizza is also excellent, especially if you like spiciness!

Everything on the menu is very good, but the pizzas are definitely the standout. My other favorite dishes are: Tagliatelle Al Uovo pasta, Sea Scallop appetizer.

I will come here again and again, not just for the food but also fun atmosphere. Everyone is attractive and well-dressed given the neighborhood.
Great food and atmosphere. Menu is slightly limited, but would come back. Highly recommend the Margherita pizza.

I have two words for this place - overrated and expensive.  The pizza was good but definitely not the best. The pasta dishes were also good but tiny, smaller than appetizers in most other restaurants.   The dessert of the day was inedible.

We only ordered two dishes - clam pizza and italian chicory salad, both of which were fantastic. The crust here is a lot more doughy even than the pizzas I had in Naples. Delicious though, if you put aside your memory of the pizzas you've had in the past. I was a bit taken aback that they only offer beer and wine, since I have a habit of getting cocktails, but the white burgundy I got was absolutely effing delicious. I strongly recommend that wine with the clam pizza.

Tasty food and solid wine selection. Had a few things things that I saw that could probably help elevate service.

The back of the house needs to remember that since it's an open kitchen, the guests are watching you. It's a performance that you have to continue until the very end. Lots of leaning, slouching and phone using. They also had a tendency of sliding and spinning their finished plates at the pass... not sure whether this is how they want to respect their finished product? 

Anyways, the group of friends and I enjoyed the food. Felt like the warmth in the staff was lacking. Id like to note that none of the front of the house staff thanked us, said goodbye or made eye contact as we were leaving. Little things like that goes a long way.

We made a reservation for 6 pm Saturday. The place is small and cozy, but they have few tables and space to accommodate slightly bigger groups too. We ordered a pie of mortodella pizza and a spaghetti monograno that had Spanish anchovy as one of the main ingredients.
The dough of the pizza was really really delicious. The spaghetti also tasted pretty good, but the portion was really not enough to make you full. I think it was mostly the pizza that made me full. I think the overall price for the dishes are slightly on the higher end, and I think there are many comparable places in the city.
I really loved the overall ambiance which can also be a really great date spot.

Food was good but not for the price. Steak was definitely not worth it. The service is rushed. They pour the wine every sip you take (then push you to buy another bottle) and rush you with each course. Clearly they were trying to move our table quickly, and they made it obvious.

This place is fantastic. Very, very elevated Italian food with great atmosphere. Pretty surreal experience eating killer Italian while listening to disco tunes. Also, this is a NO TIP RESTAURANT. So while the prices may seem high, if you deduct, say, 20% tip, the pricing is on par with many other mid tier Italian restaurants in the city.

This place is a huge hassle to get a reservation for. My girlfriend and I booked a few days in advance for an 8:45pm table on a Sunday, the only evening slot available. This was pretty late for us, so we found a number on their website that's text-only. At first I was frustrated you couldn't call them directly, but they respond very quickly to texts so fine, it works. They were able to move our reservation half an hour earlier. Nice to see they're willing to accommodate! So I definitely recommend reaching out to them after making a reservation to see if they can improve your slot.

We were seated at the table closest to the entrance. Usually I hate being placed by the entrance, especially on freezing days if the door's constantly opening and closing, but they have multiple separations between the entrance and the outside, including one of those heavy curtains around the door, so I never felt a cold draft.

We ordered the Littleneck Clam pizza and the Tortelloni pasta (made with "Corbezzolo Honey, Almond & Castelmagno Cheese"). All I can say is wow, both were fantastic.

The pizza had super thin crust, perfectly cooked. My girlfriend, who usually hates the crust, ate every bit of it. The cheese was so creamy and the flavors of clams and broccoli rabe really worked well together. The best part, which wasn't mentioned on the menu, was the side serving of chili peppers drenched in olive oil. Oh. My. God. Those peppers were fantastic! I was eating them straight from the side dish and jeez, they were so hot and sweet. Absolutely delicious. I put two or three on each slice of pizza and it was exquisite. An amazing touch and a great surprise.

The pasta was the perfect way to balance the creamy spiciness of the clam pizza. It was served in a truffle oil (once again, not on the menu) but not the cheap, doused on kind of truffle oil, but something really subtle and mixed with honey. So good. The whole bite, together with the crunch of the almonds on top, were to die for. Rich, but not sickly rich. The dish came with seven good-sized tortelloni.

Perhaps the only negative is the drinks list. Everything's expensive. Most higher end restaurants will at least have a throwaway option like a house wine or beer etc. but this place doesn't have any of that. $11 for a kölsch? Really? On the other hand, the option of sparkling water is included with your meal, which is unheard of in NYC.

Service was good too. Our waiter was charmingly aloof and our water was refilled frequently.

In the end, both dishes were incredible and I'd reorder them in a heartbeat. The whole menu looks great to be honest. I look forward to coming back and trying everything else!
Slow service - waited for 40min for one pizza and one chicken..food is ok as well not many options

We were sent here by our first choice restaurant since it had no availability. With the exception of the adorable hostess, every staff member we encountered was rude, to the point of speaking in a different language while staring at my 18 yr old daughter. The issue- they sat us at 6:00 with the agreement to make sure they would have the table back by 8:30. No problem! Well 45 minutes in, after we had ordered wine and app, we started getting questioned about when we would be done and reminders about needing the table. What?! We intended to have dinner there, even though the menu is overpriced and the by-the-glass wine selections were limited (4 reds) and none i would otherwise order. However, after this treatment, we decided to get the check and go. Left there feeling disappointed and just icky. Would not go back

The food here was fantastic. I'll just get that out of the way. We had a delicious tortalloni entree that we split as a starter because the pasta looked amazing. It was. My god, so buttery and savory with the perfect texture. Next up we split the fungi pizza and that also was delicious. The mushrooms added just the right amount of flavor and the cheesiness was tart and salty just as you'd want. This is small thing: but I even liked the wine glasses. Very light to the touch and paired nicely with the dining experience.

But now, if you've made it this far you're wondering why I've knocked off two stars. The service was very very slow. We had stopped by to put our names down and were told it would be thirty minutes. Thirty minutes later, after not having been given a text, we check in only to find that they not only forgot to put our name down but don't even remember us stopping by. We didn't have any other options so we waited it out. 

The other thing that I think is worth mentioning is hygiene of the prep chefs. I saw one man cut meat and then minutes later use that hand to sprinkle fresh Parmesan on a dish. I lost a bit of appetite after seeing that.

what a pity this restaurant has such bad service.
The food is remarkable, velvet pasta, great clam pizza, and, oh the leeks vinaigrette! However we had one server who was more interested in the table with his friends, and the second who tried very hard to please, but didn't, the pasta was not ordered with the other food, and so, when reminded I was told it was on its way. Half an hour later it appeared, and was delicious. Please, dear restaurant, put someone in charge and train your staff better, but, great food.

Popped in here for a 2 person reservation at the bar. It's located at the edge of Little Italy, and they have a small but busy spot. Wood fire pizza ovens open to see as the people work on the pizzas in front of you.

We had the appetizer of a littleneck clam pizza - the crust is super-thin at the center and bubbles up at the edges (thicker). It's interesting, garlicky, but I don't like burnt (blackened) crust at all, so not to my favor.

The tortelloni (corbezzolo honey,almond and castelmagno cheese) was fantastic - 7 pieces, though, so not a lot. The strozzapreti w/ octopus sugo was ok (pasta good, a little spicy), but the octopus was a little on the mushy side, fell apart a little too easily and lacked the slightly chewy texture that I prefer from my octopus. 

They have half bottles and full, and they were efficient with replacing plates and serving - not quite rushed but not quite relaxing, either.

Overall a busy place - I see why people like it, but I'm not a fan of blackened pizza, and the tortelloni was great.

I've been to Pasquale Jones for dinner several times in the past two years, and my more recent experiences have been fantastic (the first time I came here, it was good, but think we ordered some of the wrong things). The service, in particular, has really impressed me here. The wait staff at Pasquale Jones has always been professional, helpful, and knowledgeable, but what we really blew me away was the service we had at my most recent meal. We wanted to order a bottle of ~$60 Sauvignon Blanc that had sold out for the night -- our waiter brought over a taste of a similar wine (at the same price point) as a substitute, which I didn't love. He then came back with a $150 bottle of Sancerre, which was amazing, and they served it to us for $60 to match the original bottle I picked!! Really incredible and unexpected. 

In terms of food, their menu changes a bit seasonally, but the must order every time I'm here is the clam pizza. Sometimes we even get two, it's THAT good. Supplement that with some appetizers and pastas (I usually let our waiter steer us in this department, and have never been disappointed with their recommendations), and whatever the dessert that night is, and you will be very, very happy.
Truly wonderful food!! We had an amazing assortment of pastas and pizzas. One pizza even had clams on it. So original!! Loved the Ramona Pink Grapefruit wine spritzer too!!

This review for the Margherita pizza. I ordered this to go from Caviar, so I cannot speak to the restaurant experience.

The pizza was absolutely delicious; high quality ingredients and that fluffy bread is wonderful. I got the personal sized pizza - a little on the expensive side - but definitely worth trying!

Not sure what the low ratings are about: their pies are delicious!!

I went there with office colleagues for a team celebration, and thoroughly enjoyed the food (and drinks)! The blood-orange and fennel appetizer I ordered turned out to be the crowd favorite. But what I loved personally were the clam pizza and mushroom pizzas. Absolutely delicious, nice thin crust, and full of cheesy umami. Put a little bit of oil from the pickled chillies they give on the side (beware, spicy!) on a slice of clam pizza and you're in heaven. The rhubarb and cream fraiche dessert in the end cools down everything perfectly.

It's kinda costly, but you pay for the quality of ingredients. Totally recommended if you're a pizza lover (or anyway :p)
Awesome pizza.  Great vibe in the restaurant and would go definitely back.  My only complaint was $15 for my kids 'plain butter pasta'.

I came here literally on a whim, I wanted to treat myself to some good pizza and I saw this place packed both outside and inside. I wind up being sat easily at the bar. I believe reservations are mandatory, I'm not too sure. However I had the fluke crudo to start off with, then a glass of Sauvignon blanc. I feel bad, because I ordered the margarita pizza, but my phone died, so I gave it to the host. Which by the way the service is impeccable here, everyone is friendly and helpful too. I got the pizza and it was delicious. They cook the food right in front of you. The tomato sauce was absolutely delicious. The head chef she was very accommodating with answering my questions about he substitution for that night for the original crudo that's on the menu. The fluke crudo I had as a starter was very delicious and fresh mint sprigs with I believe scallions made it refreshing. I demolished my pizza I was super hungry lol.. however I do recommend this place to many others, because the food is very good. I will be back here with a few more friends, but I do appreciate the hospitality. Also when closing out my bill when trying to tip, I found out the tip is included in the "hospitality." Haven't seen that in a very long time. Thank you for your service.

I read up on NYC pizza and this place kept popping up so we listened. It was one of the best pizzas I ever had. The Clam pizza. We sat outside at the perfect table. Drank a perfect glass of Spritzer and dined in the perfect setting Little Italy.

Had a lovely lunch here consisting of the margherita and clam pizzas. The clam pizza is really special with lots of clam and cream and a delicious chewy crust.  Also I shared the braised leeks with walnuts.  Some leeks were a little underdone and the dish was very rich - in a good way.  Will be back for the pizza, though the place is a little pricey (regardless of included tip).

Great food, service and ambiance. Reasonable pricing for the neighborhood, although the artichoke salad was pretty small and nothing to write home about for the price. Wish they had a full bar, but overall quality of food and service makes up for that! Lamb was perfect, recommend!
Best pizza around. Taste of Italy. Incredible charred asparagus with burrata. Ran out of pasta but service was amazing and they gave us great wine.

In Little Italy where you can trip and fall into an Italian restaurant, exists Pasquale Jones. On the corner, with outside seating, a kitchen bar where you can gaze into the wood burning pizza oven, you can enjoy the menu items. I had the Pizza Diavolo and it was tasty. Good for groups, service was prompt, wine menu. People watch while eating good pizza!

Pasquale Jones is Charlie Bird with pizza. What does that mean? When you dine at Pasquale Jones you are getting great flavors, great music and great service. 

I have a theory as to why this restaurant is getting some low reviews. Sometimes, people follow guides of trusted reviewers more than they follow their gut. For example, my sister read online that you should definitely order the clam pizza to optimize your dining experience at Pasquale Jones. My sister does not like clams, but my sister ordered the clam pizza. Why? I have no idea. She hated it and decided she hated the restaurant. The takeaway: order food that actually appeals to you. 

When we arrived we were greeted by the friendly host and seated immediately. The service was great here. I recently started wondering if I was just becoming harsh when it comes to restaurant service because I have had a lot of complaints at places I've been dining at lately. We dined here and I realized, no, I'm not harsh, these restaurants just haven't perfected their service formulas. Overall, the waiters were attentive and knowledgeable. A+

THE FOOD: We ordered the Artichoke Toast, the asparagus with burrata, the Margarita pizza, the Pea Shoot pizza and the English Pea Agnolotti. This menu is changing with the seasons so some of these items may not be on your menu, but they were all delicious. My personal favorites were the English Pea Agnolotti as well as the Pea shoot Pizza (I like peas). 

Overall, I absolutely loved this restaurant and would go back. My advice when dining here is to order what you think you would enjoy, not what some person who has dined at a lot of restaurants is encouraging you to order.

I was unimpressed. The food wasn't terrible. But it wasn't all that either. I got the diavolo pizza and it was tasty. But the crust had a burnt taste and was soggy in the middle. Also the service was meh at best. There was a level of snootyness from almost every staff member except the hostess, as if they were doing us a favor to allow us to eat at their restaurant. Overall it was an overpriced and underwhelming experience.

Spent a lot of money and got kicked out. 

4 person reservation - 2 were on time and 2 were 40 min late due to a delayed flight. We put the full order in 30 min after sitting, so that the food would be ready not long after the other 2 arrived.. however the food 
 came out another 40 min after ordering. 

We order 2 apps, 2 pizzas, 3 pastas, 2 entrees, and 3 $150+ bottles of wine. 

Waiter presented the check when they cleared our entrees. We asked to order dessert and was told no...  we have to leave because our 2 hour allotment was up.

On one hand I respect that others reserved the table, but this could have been handled better. We spent/ordered a lot and how we were respectful while there (not loud / not rowdy). Offering to move us to the bar or even dessert to go would have been better than telling us we needed to leave.

The food was good but the service was pretty bad. The waiter was pretty agro and impatient. We ordered a few glasses of wine. The pour on the prosecco was tiny and he switched the wine on us so the price on the first glass was $14 and it went up to $25. He laughed when we asked about it. Maybe they should bring back tipping. It ruined the meal. It's a shame because we liked this place.

Had come here before many many months ago and it was amazing. Returned for dinner. The waiter told us to order way too many things which is fine but when we ordered what we wanted and the amount we wanted, he laughed and said "ha okay fine but I know you will order more". We did not end up ordering more. The way in which he said that was weirdly condescending. 

Then they came back more than an hour later saying they ran out of a pasta. We had someone on the table with a serious nut allergy, and asked for everything without nuts. They then messed up 2 plates which we had to return. 

The food itself was good, and we were fine with the high prices because the tip was already included (although clearly this seemed to preclude the server from caring if anything was done right or even having basic kindness)

Then the bill comes. We pay. He brings me someone else's credit card!! That's mistake number 5 already and it's a big one! What if someone got my credit card - they could have taken off! I told him and he took it back without even caring! 

Then he returns, we sign the check without tip, as it was all included.

He takes it, and puts the pen back near it, adding insult to injury stating: "We no longer have tip included".

Now this is very strange for many reasons: 
1. The menu states this is a no tipping establishment
2. There is a yelp review from SIX days ago talking about not tipping!! 
3. The prices are still sky high on their menu!

Although this place used to be good, the attitude of the server literally ruined the taste of the food. AND I'm not sure if we were conned by him. We tipped because there are other staff that likely rely on tipping money but I couldn't help but feeling pretty horrible about the whole experience.

I don't write bad reviews. I can't believe the dinner was so bad that I had to write this one. Will not be returning.

I was really excited to eat here. A friend had mentioned that it was great and that they practiced the no-tipping policy as tip was included in each item cost (also evidenced by some of the menu pics posted here on yelp.) 

We arrived (group of 6), waiter made a recommendation to share everything family style by ordering 4 shared plates, 2 pizzas and 3 pastas. We followed suit, except we got 2 pastas as 2 of the four pasta dishes had meat. We explained we had a nut allergy and vegetarians at the table. When the apps come out the tomato dish had nuts all over it. He apologizes and takes the dish back and brings a new dish with no nuts some time later. We are at least 30-40min out from placing our initial order when the waiter comes back to tell us we can't have one of the pasta dishes we ordered as they ran out with no solution or alternate recommendation. We obviously have not ordered enough food- even by his own initial recommendation if we are only going to have one pasta dish among the 6 of us. He does not come back to our table for the next 5 minutes. Another waiter/possible manager notices that my eyes are darting around the restaurant looking for our waiter and senses something is wrong. I explain that it is not acceptable for them to let us know 30-40min later into our meal that one of the main entrees is no longer available especially since half of our table is vegetarian and there are no other meatless pastas. He says that he will see what he can do and making our originally ordered pasta dish shouldn't be a problem they may just need to use different mushrooms. No problem- at least a solution has been presented. The food arrives. The pastas are definitely not meant to be shared. The artichoke tortelli has maybe 6 or 7 small tortelli (think 1.5 size of a tortellini.)
When it comes time to pay the bill there were six of us, we placed 6 credit cards down. Waiter takes the cards and doesn't say anything. He comes back 10 minutes later and says "our system is currently down and can only take up to 3 cards at a time." No problem. he then comes back after he runs the credit card. We sign and are getting ready to leave but waiting while people in our party use the bathroom. When he notices that there is no tip he proceeds to come back and *demand* a tip stating they are no longer a "no-tipping" restaurant. Buddy- you should gage your audience, you've messed up so many times at this point it would be in your best interest to just let us leave peacefully and not cause any further commotion. I highly doubt you demanding that we leave tip was worth having this yelp review posted because that was the icing on top of everything that has directed me to come here and comment.

The main theme of my complaint is timeliness and attitude. I felt like our waiter wasted a lot of our time and after the nut allergy mess up, which he did apologize for- was not apologetic for other mess ups. I know there are two sides to everything and I have worked in restaurants before which likely raises my level of scrutiny, but from the beginning getting a nut allergy wrong, not knowing that a pasta dish wasn't available and not offering any solution or recommendation. To the credit cards. To the attitude demanding tip. Pasquale Jones I wanted to like you but you need to raise your standards and expectations for your front of house staff. 

TLDR;food was ok but not up to its price point and service not up to speed for the ambiance they are trying to deliver.
Had a light second dinner here. Food was solid. Wine selection was tasty. Service was a bit lackluster. Might be worth to check it out. Loved the airiness to the restaurant.

Really yummy pizza with fluffy crust. If you like clams definitely get the clam pizza. The restaurant has nice vibes inside, modern and big booths for parties of around 5. The pizza is totally worth coming for.

I used to love this place. I would have given it 5 Stars a year ago. I've been numerous times since it opened and was always excited to come back. Only 1 time prior to this was the food really not great (and it seemed to be a night the chef, Timothy Caspere, was not in). We let it go. 

First, they took the pork shank - one of the best dishes I've had in ages - off the menu. Even after they raised it $10+ we always ordered it. 

Second, this has been a no-tipping establishment for ages. So even when they raised prices after the initial opening, it seemed fair enough. I took 4 friends here on Saturday (with the intention to pay our own way), and told them specifically that the prices baked in tip. The menu did not indicate otherwise. The waiter did not asked if we'd dined with them before and proceed to update us on policy. It only became clear at the end of the meal when we got the bill and I noticed that a line for Tip had magically appeared where there had never been one previously. And this is after ordering 2 pretty pricey bottles of wine that I reasoned were not overpriced because of the tipping policy.
