I got up and asked the hostess. She informed me the policy had changed less than 1 month ago. That was it. She didn't let the waiter know I had asked. No apology or hint of apologetic tone. It's not on the menu, or the website or their Instagram. Just sneaking it in -- we now pay 20% more for food that has honestly gone downhill over the last year.  I'm sad to write this review because it was one of my favorite places in the city. But I don't think I'll be going back.

Reservations are hard to get but worth the effort. In a group of 5 we got: 
- some like cracker with ricotta spread. Cracker was meh but the ricotta stuff was amazing. 5 stars. 
- braised leeks: pretty good
- we might have gotten the tomato and mozzarella starter too? I forget 
- we got three pizzas which were really good, yes floppy: margherita, diavola, & Norma. The Norma does have meat on it but my generally non red meat eating friend didn't think it tasted to meaty. 
- Tortelli pasta: it was good to share, but rich is not sure I would have wanted the full serving myself. 
- fish of the day was bass: it was fine. 
- side of peppers: also fine but not special. 
- dessert: guess they always have one per day, which is like a fruit crumble with ice cream. This day the fruit was blueberries and the ice cream was vanilla and it was so good!! It was actually quite large too, which was surprising. We got two of these :-p 

Music is good too. Definitely a happening spot that I'd recommend but probs won't be back too soon.
I had an incredible experience at PJ, this is by far my favorite restaurant in NYC. The food is mouthwatering, and the service is impeccable. I will definitely be coming back.

Been dying to check our Pasquale Jones for a year, have read great things. Decided to give it a go tonight and got a table early. Long story short the restaurant itself is very nice, food is ok, just ok, portions are small, service was friendly and nice, if a little over attentive, once we put a glass down it was swept off the table , prices are extortionate, can of Kolsche - 10 dollars!!! COME ON! 

Overall it was grand, wouldn't go back, waaaaay too pricy for what you get. Go to Speedy Romeos.

We like this place but today was aweful. Food was the usual but their aircon was broken. Wood fire ovens were pumping out hot air and the whole place was worse than being in subway station in August. Couldn't wait to get out. 

Honestly shut the damn place down rather than subjecting your patrons to this torture

Okay experience here after wanting to try for a while! We got the diavolo pizza and cavatelli. Diavolo was very salty, would've been nice to have some more tomato flavor. Cavatelli was good.

Side note, I wanted to add some balsamic on the pizza to cut the saltiness, so asked the waiter, but he said they couldn't provide any since they only use the fancy kind in the kitchen. Not sure what that means when they use a fancy kind to cook but can't give some to customers. Maybe they could buy a cheap one to provide on the side when people ask? Just a thought.

Five stars for the little neck clam pizza!!! This was easily the standout dish at this small but hip restaurant in Nolita. The pastas were good but not great. It could be because I was not as hungry towards the end of my meal. The scallops were delicious and I would recommend getting them as a starter. Would definitely come back here again for that clam pizza!
The pizza is okay, but the apps and pasta are delicious.  The agnolotti were probably the best filled pasta I've ever had.  Atmosphere is loud and friendly.
We had outdoor dining because it was really nice out. The Margherita pizza and little neck clam pie is to die for but way too overpriced for its size. I also like it because I like thin crust pizza.

Pasquale Jones was a nice restaurant with a good environment and friendly staff. The staff were attentive, so if you don't like plates being moved immediately then just be aware of that. The pizzas were tasty, but our favorite was the Sweetcorn Agnolotti pasta. It was delicious and buttery. The wine list was good, but cheapest bottle was $55. Overall, a good place to go that might be a little overpriced.

we ordered three things, but this rating is for the clam pizza and the clam pizza ONLY. the other ones flew over my head (tongue) simply bc they were outshined by this pizza. from the hot, chewy crust to the little chili peppers and lemon they give you to complement this dish - it was a delight in every bite. 

clam pizza huh who would've THUNK. my bf made the rezy to this place called pasquale jones saying he found something he wanted to try. once he mentioned clam pizza my face scrunched up with a questionable look, but y'know, food is food, and if it's good they'll make it work. 

IM SO GLAD THEY DID~~ if there's one dish you want to order, it's this one. i crave this pizza one too many times

Delicious pasta (I had the caccio e Pepe), however... I did a takeout order from here a week ago (when I had the pasta) and ordered their burrata with chili oil and asked for a side of bread. The order came with NO CHILI OIL (the whole premise of the burrata dish) and no bread, just kale.... super frustrating.
Did not impress me one bit. Food was ok but not worth the price and definitely didn't live up to the hype.

Went to this place for dinner with a group of friends, food was EXCELLENT and the ambiance was great. The 3/5 stars is for the poor service! 

Food: we got several starters including warm ricotta and caprese salad. These both were amazing. The drink menu is wine and bar only, but very good selection of wines including bottles that pair well. For dinner the pizza and pastas are GREAT. Had several so I forget the names but all in all, excellent. 

Ambiance: good for date nights but also a close group of friends like 4-6. We had 5 in our group and sat well in a booth. 

Service: now the sole reason for the 3/5. The waiter was ridiculous, he came by several times to ask what we'd like to order when we looked unsure/ready to ask questions - he left. Only when we were 'completely' ready then he took it. We ordered a pizza asking for it to be vegetarian without 'little fish' but it came out with the fish. When confronting the waiter about it, he said no they aren't there. So we had to dissect the pizza and show him!! Then when we had the pizza remade, the chefs took liberty to add olives instead which we said we ONLY want the fish removed, nothing else. 

Great food and ambiance for a nice date night, but I will probably will never come back due to the terrible service with other options in the city.

Horrific experience. Was really looking forward to dining here with my husband, but unfortunately our waiter made this experience horrendous. First, the waiter took 45 minutes just to notice we had been seated and take our order. We waited about another 45 minutes in between each dish which was painful. He never checked in with us once asking if we were okay. Then he left out two of the dishes we ordered completely, and brought us the check (which charged us for the 2 dishes he forgot!) Rather than apologizing for the 2 missing dishes, he said "It is your fault you missed two dishes because you eat too fast." Have no idea what that even means or how the speed at which one eats affects whether dishes come out of the kitchen. Won't ever be going back here again for sure and will definitely let all my friends know how horribly we were treated and how disrespectful the staff was to us.

Pasquale Jones is extremely overrated. 

Issue 1: We had a reservation at 9:15pm and were not seated until 9:45pm. This is unusual even for New York.

Issue 2: We ordered a bottle of wine. The waiter returned with the wrong bottle. We had to point this out. He went to retrieve the right bottle, came back to tell us they were out, and tried to sell us the original wrong bottle which he was still holding. We eventually ordered something else.

Issue 3: We ordered the Littleneck Clam and Pomodorino pizzas, which took about 40 minutes to come out (so over an hour after our reservation until we got any food). Both pizzas were just barely acceptable - more crust than topping and the crust itself was decent but quite burnt.

Prices are a bit high for what you get. Service is inattentive. That would be ok if the food were good, but the pizzas were ok at best and certainly nothing remotely close to special. I guess people like the ambience...
Food was great. I would definitely come back for the food.Reason for the 4 was because the hostess is very rude. He had attitude not very friendly welcoming.

Great potential with a very responsive staff and good location.  Unfortunately the pasta was undercooked and the sauce that the waiter said was spicy was the most bland pasta sauce I've had in years.  Skip this place and start with the gelato shop across the street.

If I could give minus stars I would (and I'm a very generous rater). TERRIBLE customer service! They have NO INTEGRITY and don't take care of their patrons after they've caused injury resulting in needing dental work done.

Dined here a few months ago and ordered their famous littleneck clam pizza. Everything was going really well as it usually does (have been here lots before). Great vibes and wine with a GF. We sat at the bar, facing the open kitchen near the washrooms.

Unfortunately, they were not thorough enough with the pizza because when I bit down on a clam slice, I chomped on a clamshell! It messed up my tooth and couldn't eat on that side for the rest of the night. The manager, Danny, came by after we let the server know and was very apologetic. He gave me his card, took the pizza off and said if it continues to cause issues, to let him know as they have insurance. After going to the dentist who then referred me to an endodontist, since the pain and tenderness had not subsided after a week, it was diagnosed that it needed a root canal (it was monitored for a couple more weeks in case it was just a bruised nerve). I emailed Danny (who required several follow ups to respond). He asked for an account of what happened and if I had seen the dentist. After providing him with documentation, he seemingly was empathetic and apologetic, saying it was a terrible situation that he wanted to get resolved. He (apparently) passed everything onto his management who then (apparently) submitted to their insurance company. After a few more follow ups to check on the status over the next few weeks then turned months, they GHOSTED. No more communications. NOTHING. I gave them the benefit of the doubt it was the insurance company taking a long time as he had said, "it's in the hands of the insurance company". I asked for the claim number or any details so I could follow up. NOTHING. Several follow ups later and still nothing. 

I understand that it was an honest mistake but it should be rectified. Customers should not have to pay for damages caused by eating at an establishment - especially when it's at the negligence of the restaurant. Extremely disappointed because I loved going to this place but if you're not going to take care of your customers and lie to them instead, you're not getting my business.

KenScale: 8.5/10

Throughout my culinary experience in New York City, there are a few restaurants where I had a great experience but somehow I ended up not going in a while. Perhaps that is because of so many choices in the diverse dining scene in the city. Perhaps I'm becoming more forgetful as I age. In any event, it was only recently that I realized, when searching for a restaurant to have dinner with a foodie friend visiting from out of town (along with our mutual friend as well as my lovely wife Jun), that for some inexplicable reasons, I had only been to Pasquale Jones once back in 2016. As my friend, an avid food blogger who writes with a lot more flourish than mine, was on a semi-business trip to check out Italian restaurants around the city for a new restaurant project that she was consulting for, I thought Pasquale Jones would be a perfect place to show her the type of casual yet really good restaurant. And I'm glad that the restaurant is still hitting  on all cylinders.

Since the foodie friend had a very generous expense account budget, she ordered perhaps a bit too much food for a party of four, but we didn't complain (I had a very light lunch that day at work knowing that we'll probably get a bunch of dishes). The two giant wood-fire ovens and the pizzas that come out of them are still the highlights of the restaurant's menu, but don't sleep on their appetizers, such as the refreshing fluke crudo or the Montauk scallops with corn, butter bean and sweet pepper that I regretted were a bit too small (because they were quite delicious and I was in no mood for sharing one). The vegetables were also fantastic, such as the charred Romano beans with spring onion and pancetta that showed robust texture and the warm braised leeks with toasted walnut and Parmigiano. The two pasta dishes were also solid, especially the sweetcorn agnolotti with chanterelle mushroom and Parmigiano that Jun remarked could a fantasy for every pasta-loving girl for its sweet flavor and wonderfully al dente texture. It was really in the pizza department, however, that Pasquale Jones still shines, and I'm very close to declaring this might be one of the top five pizza destinations in Manhattan. The signature littleneck clam pie with garlic, lemon and broccoli rabe was fantastic as always, but the best one of the night probably belonged to the squash blossom pie with zucchini, basil and "little fish" that the server described as a type of anchovy. I was very impressed with the generous vegetable toppings that worked together beautifully for a semi-healthy flavor. The other two pizzas (as mentioned above, we ordered a lot!) were also very good; I loved the spicy kick coming from the hot pepper in diavola pie, and the burrata cheese in the other pie displayed a ton of freshness that Jun very much liked. As if the four pies weren't enough, the foodie friend wanted to order one secondi dish, and I remembered that the restaurant's pork shank (available as an off-menu item during our visit) was supposed to be one of its best dishes. It was indeed a wise decision to order this beautiful meat dish, with impeccable texture without overpowering flavor. If all four of us hadn't been stuffed from the massive carb intakes previously, I have no doubt we would've finished this in five minutes. Just like last time, there is only dessert available at Pasquale Jones on a given day, and I suggest never skipping one at the restaurant as the dessert usually involves roasted fruit. On our visit, roasted apricot accompanied by raspberry and vanilla gelato was available and everyone really enjoyed this delightful dish that wasn't overly sweet.

Pasquale Jones is still a very popular restaurant where securing a table at prime time can be a challenge so plan ahead accordingly. On a weekday dinner, the restaurant certainly seems to have more younger crowds than the last time I had visited on a Sunday when I saw a couple of families with kids hanging out together. The wine list comes from various places around the world; ordering a glass or bottle of red Italian should be the way to go if you are inclined to have some alcohol to complement the food. I'm still not sure to this day how I never managed to revisit Pasquale Jones after a memorable first meal, but I have no doubt I will use this restaurant again for future occasions.

HANNAH greeted us when we walked in and was absolutely delightful. She was so super friendly with a huge smile, and you could tell she genuinely enjoyed what she was doing. Everyone who walked in was welcomed this way and she continued to impress us with her exceptional customer service throughout he evening. Food was amazing and so flavorful. We ended up ordering another pizza because it was so good!  Definitely swing in here for amazing food and outstanding customer service - THANK YOU Hannah  You made up for all the crappy service we received earlier in the day.  Xo

Food is amazing.  This is normally one of favorite
restaurants in NY.  Service was exceptionally poor last visit with smug host and server.  Waited 10 minutes for a first approach then got poured a glass of wine that I actually thought was just for me to taste but it was the entire glass.   Crazy.
PIZZA. Get it!!! They cook it beautifully and the service is great.  Ambiance for mid day lunch had a good vibe. Well situated in Little Italy district.

Such a great food experience here. The ABSOLUTE must order is the sweet corn agnolotti. Blows all other pasta I've had in NYC out of the park. Also, the grilled octopus was cooked perfectly. We also got the tagliatelle with Ragu which was great, the burrata starter (which was really good but if I had to eliminate something it would be that), the clam pizza and diavola pizza. Only two downfalls are they moved a little slowly (but well worth it) and they only had ONE bottle of red on the menu less than $

Was craving pizza... craving satisfied. We got the prosciutto one. Love the tender but chewy crust and the prosciutto on the pizza was 100. Also had burrata which was super creamy and yummy w the delicata squash and hazelnuts. Not the place to go if you're craving a New York slice but if youre Pasquale jonesin' for the good stuff, it's the joint.

I love this restaurant for several reasons: 

1. It has great pizza, everything we've had has been good here. Our go-tos are the Diavolo and the Margarita. 
2. I can make a reservation to eat this great pizza, instead of standing in a line for 40 minutes to eat it in the street. 
3. This place is popular (if you walk-in night of you'll have at least an hour wait if not more) but not so insanely popular that I have to stay up until midnight 30 days before my desired dinner date, refreshing the Resy website and scrambling to get a reservation time at a decent hour. I have great affection for excellent restaurants that aren't so, so stressful to get into. 
4. It's located in such a fun part of town, it is breezy to have dinner here and then walk to your next location. 
5. They have a nice wine list, so you can enjoy good wine with your delicious pizza. Sometimes it really is the little things. Also, it's nice without being fussy which is my favorite. 
6. The service is always great, we never have any complaints.

Get ready for the rudeness the second you walk in the door. Very bad attitude and they are not welcoming! Owners need to pay attention to all of the negative reviews about front of the house.  I gave this place 3 chances because the pizza is good although a little pricy. 
I will never ever return to this restaurant again because there are many good restaurants in NYC who respect and appreciate their customers.
Ps. A glass of wine $18 serving just 2 sips. Really!!!!
Service was good food was subpar, ordered pizza, pasta, and ricotta appetizer. Appetizer was the best item we ordered.

Pasquale Jones invigorates classic pizza and amps up Italian-inspired flavors via their two incredible wood burning ovens. It's the kind of casual, Italian dining that fits today's style perfectly: easy to share, unique and innovative dishes. The quality is strong, and I believe even better than a year or two ago. Naturally, the pizzas are not to be missed, but don't overlook the wood-fired mains. Wine aficionados will not be disappointed, as the list contains an interesting array of off-beat names and heavy-hitters. On a chilly fall evening, a spot at the counter next to the wood burning ovens was heaven.

Atmosphere
- The space is small, so expect tables that are closely spaced.
- My favorite seating is the counter by the ovens, overlooking the open kitchen. You get a prime view and it doesn't feel as cramped.
-Lively and fun, a cool place to hang out.

Food
What doesn't taste better coming from a wood burning oven? Every order must include at least one "Neo-NY" pizza. While it may be natural to gravitate toward the pastas to go with, in my opinion the shareable starters are some of the best dishes on the menu. On our visit we enjoyed:

- Warm Braised Leeks (Toasted Walnut & Parmigiano Reggiano - $16): A classic, loaded with parmesan that melds into the braised leeks. The leeks take on a velvety texture and the cheese is of very high quality. Such an awesome fall dish.
- Maple-Glazed Delicata Squash (Brussels Sprout, Horseradish & Caraway - $19): Maybe a touch overpriced, but very well composed and nicely balanced. The caraway was a surprising element that helped freshen up the heavy veg.
- Brussels Sprout Pizza (Red Onion, Smoked Mozzarella & Lemon - $22): Love the crust here, neither too heavy nor too thin and just the right amount of salt. Excellent combination of high quality toppings.
- Heritage Berkshire Pork Chop (Chestnut & Brussels Sprout - $36): Perhaps the least innovative of what we got, nevertheless tasty and good quality cut. Well cooked, though.
- Braised Pear with Vanilla Gelato ($14): No dessert menu per se, but this special was a simple, well executed finish. Flavorful and nicely done, though certainly overpriced - perhaps easier to accomplish with no printed menu?

Beverage
Wine list is very interesting. It's surprisingly lengthy, and has good span across regions and types. For wine geeks, pretty cool and not to be missed! The list includes a heavy selection vintage picks, thought to be perfectly honest, some of these are head-scratchers in this sort of venue. Maybe some do enjoy a $2,200 Montrachet with their pie... it's NYC after all. Anyway, I was very pleased to find the 2015 Conterno Barbera d'Alba Vigna Cerretta ($130), a very high quality offering and paired perfectly with the food. The markup was also quite reasonable.

Service
- Very friendly and attentive throughout our experience. 
- Pacing on the food could be a bit slow when they get busy.

Pizza and pasta are both highly regarded but the calzone napoletana was amazing. If you like Italian meats you really must try it. Great place for all to visit - date, parents from out of town. Go wander down mulberry afterwards and get some dessert.

Would not go back. Can have pizzas and pastas in a million other places with far better service. Really unprofessional. 

Food was good enough. Clam pizza was good and braised leeks were excellent. The rest was good but not particularly memorable. 

But it was all overshadowed by the poor service. Very disappointing.
Note to self and those sensitive to spice babies like myself. The salami tastes spicy now. Is it me, is it a different brand now, who knows, but consider this a PSA.

The pizza is pretty good here, although some may not find it to be the perfect New York pizza joint. The crust is slightly crispy, but still has a floppy composure. The Diavola pizza is good, has very little sauce, and is slightly spicy (there are peppers on the pizza which may make it too spicy for some).   The pizza is somewhat small, and likely can be enjoyed entirely by one person. If ordering for two, you should get either two pizzas or a pizza and a separate dish.

Solid pizza located at the heart of soho. Felt like I was paying more for the ambience. We got the clam, funghi, and margherita. 

Clam pizza is a must.

Went today for lunch- stumbled in, because the wait everywhere else was insane. This restaurant was a pleasant surprise! We tried two different pizzas, the fresh catch and brown butter sage agnolotti. Everything we had was delicious. The pizza was fantastic- fresh, quality ingredients, a light and flavorful tomato sauce, excellent wood fired crust. They serve it with a spicy chili oil on the side, which takes it to the next level. The pasta tasted fresh, and the brown butter sage sauce was delicious. Their fresh catch was seared, flaky, and served with a light shaved fennel and citrus salad.

The meal was honestly a little pricey, but everything was delicious. We sat at the bar and enjoyed watching the open kitchen.

Recommend for bar or table service, don't skip the pizza or pasta.

This is one of my favorite restaurants not just because of the food (which is excellent and never have i left disappointed) but because i have gotten some of the best service here. I first started going to Pasquale alone on my lunch break. When i craved thin, spicy, delicious soppressata pizza this was my go-to. They do it just right with fresh mint and a side container of hot chili oil you can add to your desired spiciness. And it's HOT! Soon i became a regular and i was served by BABA. He was always so humble and sweet. I started coming with my friends for dinners and was pleased that he was now working dinner service as well! On a few occasions when i first started coming in i will admit the manager who also worked the reservations was not always so gracious and did make me feel uncomfortable repeatedly. BABA out-weighed out this experience ten-fold though. Recently, at dinner i was assisted by Jacob who was the polar opposite of the not so inviting manager i spoke prior of. Jacob was warm and SO accommodating. He helped me get seated in my beloved BABA'S section. In conclusion the food here is always delicious. I recommend any of the starters as they never disappoint. The PASTA'S are all phenomenal and I really enjoy sitting at the bar and watching the cook staff prepare! The wine list is also great! Not to big and overwhelming but with a nice round selection to choose from. I make it a point to only come when BABA'S working.

Food is excellent twist on Italian food.  The pizza is amazing.  The sauce is so good.  Kind of pricey, but a nice spot to stop at for date night.  I recommend just sitting at the bar.  It's cool to watch the guys cook and they are very friendly

So we took a chance and ordered a pizza for delivery 
Pizza showed up late and ice cold
Delivery was through a company called Caviar
Customer support was a $10 credit towards future delivery 
We tried to explain that does no good since we don't live in NYC
SO bottom line is Caviar tasted more like SPAM

They burned me once , never again

DONT get pizza delivered unless you want to cook it yourself.  Had pizza delivered through caviar (only app available to deliver from this place) and pizza arrived COLD with instructions on reheating.  Contacted caviar via text return responses which sounded robotic and unhelpful.  They offered a credit for my next delivery. Next delivery?  I've learned my lesson, and just hoping to save you the same trouble.  Too bad I can't review the food.

The lobster arrabiata is NOT a pasta. It's a crepe. And a tiny one. For $28. I'm talking 3 bites. And it's under the pasta section so it is extremely deceiving. We were super disappointed. Love Pasquale Jones but this menu item was a no go for us. Pizza good as always. We would have sent it back if we could.

Pasquale Jones has been on my list for some time, and I finally came here for dinner last week with a friend. We made a reservation on Resy a couple of days before, and the reservation was easy to get. 
They have a big outdoor dining section which is fully covered, with overhead heating. The staff are all in masks, and you scan a QR code to get the menu. The two of us weren't very hungry, so we got one appetizer, and one pizza to share. This amount of food was good for the both of us. 
The food was presented not long after we ordered. The warm braised leeks were served in butter and parmesan, and were warm, simple and comforting. 
We ordered the clam pizza as it is their signature pizza. It's a clam pizza without sauce, broccoli rabe and cream, garlic and lemon. It was delicious, and cooked well. Dough was great. 
Service was very attentive, warm and friendly. Would recommend this place for pizza in the Little Italy area.
The best Italian I've had in Manhattan. Amazing food, everything from the pasta, and pizza to the chocolate cake, and our service was fantastic. Eric was awesome! Will absolutely be back again!

A night of firsts and last. The first being the only time I have ever left an Italian restaurant hungry! And the last being that I will never return to this poor excuse for a restaurant.  THIS IS A TOURIST TRAP. It's overpriced, with extremely tiny portions and bad service that just takes advantage of the fact they are on Mulberry Street to bring tourists in. I'm honestly in shock.. My friend and I had two glasses of wine each and each had the cacio de pepe pasta for $125 plus tip and we were left astonished.. The pasta serving was 4 bites.. we counted.. and freezing cold.. Seriously?? I've never left an Italian restaurant hungry in my life. I honestly went right home and made a bowl of soup, I wasn't about to spend more money on the nothingness they serve. You would think they would be smart enough to serve bread (which I never normally eat to leave room but would have killed for tonight) to trick people into being full but no... they care about tourists money, not leaving customers full and happy. I couldn't get the check fast enough. Do not waste your time and money.

Their food and environment is ok but the little things earned this place 3 stars.  No ice tea, no drip coffee, no bread for the burrata.  The Cacio e peppe was excessively cheesy which granted some people might like. Also the sausage pizza was just cheese and sausage and I wish it would have had some tomato sauce on it. The last thing is that the topping to crust ratio is a little off.  The Caesar salad needed more dressing too

Oh my God, Pasquale Jones was simply astonishing. I was left speechless. We are so pleased that we have purchased Diavola, it was really wonderful. Team are really lovely and service is really fast. If I am ever in the area again I will love to come back to Pasquale Jones.

Loved their Neapolitan style pizza. Great grower champagne list. Skip the yellow tail crudo and meatballs. Stick with pizza! The waiter was very informative, friendly and unobtrusive. Check out their wood fired oven. Love the outdoor set up and powerful heaters (for cooler nights).  Oh, and they use Zalto glasses.

Pasta tasted like a kid's menu pasta and it was very hard (raw). I complained and nothing happened. It was also very expensive. Pizza (from
The table next to mine) looked good.

The food was absolutely delicious. A perfect spot to come with friends!
The burrata was tasty and came with wonderful sourdough bread and greens. The ravioli was perfectly sweet and the mushrooms complimented them so well! We also got the special, scallops, that were perfectly cooked, and crisped on the top, plus the flavors were super complimenting to the natural flavor of the scallop. Lastly, we got a Margherita pizza which was Neapolitan, but NOT floppy, which was awesome! 
In conclusion: yes, I would absolutely recommend visiting Pasquale Jones

This place was recommended by the DK guide to NYC so we walked the entire length of Mulberry street to get to it.
Checked out the wine list and ordered two glasses of wine for $30, not especially impressive.
The leek appetizer looked interesting and was tasty but $18 for small plate of leeks and and a few tiny potato slices seemed excessive.   We had to ask for bread.
The entree also disappointing. A cup or so of pasta in a cream sauce with TWO shrimp for $30! I know this is NYC but this was not a tasting   menu item but a full  entree. It was very unimpressive in taste. Very bland. 
At over a $100  we left hungry and frustrated. As we walked back down Mulberry Street we saw people enjoying generous plates of delicious looking  pasta I regretted my restaurant choice for my only meal in Little Italy.
Avoid this place.

Everything from the wine to the pizza was delicious. The wine director Theo suggested a perfect wine and red bottle for our group of 5 women, we were all obsessed with how good both were. We asked for suggestions on apps and the wine director and server both said the leeks were amazing. They were good, don't get me wrong, but did not compare to the buratta with tangy pea shoots on top and bread grilled in butter. The fennel sausage, diavola and pea shoot pizza (couldn't stay away from those damn delicious pea shoots) were all exquisite! 

The restaurant itself wasn't overly busy for a Friday night which was a bonus!

We came for dinner on a Wednesday, and I was surprised by how packed the restaurant was. The restaurant showcases its two large stone pizza ovens. The tables were packed together (even during COVID)- I could not even be seated without intruding on the table adjacent to us. It was also difficult to hold a conversation while dining without being drowned out by the loud music and other noises. The restaurant is nicely decorated, but you should be prepared for packed seating and loud music. 

We ordered the Margherita pizza and the Casoncelli (with wood-roasted corn, oyster mushrooms, and ricotta). Both entrees were great: the quality of pasta was amazing and the dough used for their pizzas was chewy and nicely baked. However, I felt that the portion size of the pasta dishes was too small. Although it was meant to be a main dish, I felt the portion was more like an appetizer. 

Overall, I wasn't too impressed by Pasquale Jones. I thought the service was good and the food was good, but for the prices they have, I don't think I would come again. Many other amazing Italian restaurants in Little Italy have a better ambiance and have better prices.

This restaurant is perfect for a higher end, chill dinner with a younger crowd. While the restaurant is clearly upscale, it's nothing you have to dress too crazy nice for or show off at. The wait staff is exceptional and you can see all of the food being made in the kitchen right behind the tables. The music was modern pop which made it trendier (it was also at a louder but still reasonable volume). The food was on the whole quite good but my one critique is the price point-- especially considering this restaurant is right in little Italy, the pricing was steep for the value.
The food was good but not worth their expensive prices. We ordered pizzas and Prosecco. Make reservations because it's very crowded. The outdoor space as fun vibes but in a busy area.

Pizza and pasta is a combo I did not know I needed until I tried it for the first time a couple months ago. This time though it was a more of pizza party theme, as we had the widely praised littleneck clam and the diavola. Both were solid choices, with the broccoli rabe's bitterness balancing the fattiness of the cream and sour citrus of lemon giving the edge to the clam pizza, personally my first of the kind. The two pizzas, despite their petite size, proved too much for our collective appetite after our braised leek salad, which was a dark horse candidate for the best dish of all.

I dropped by Pasquale Jones for a weekend lunch with a friend and were somewhat surprised to arrive to an empty dining room at noon sharp. The tables would fill up slowly over the course of our meal, but the ambience was nowhere near what it would be during dinner service. The music was bumping, which would suit the evening crowd, but was just a few decibels too much in the daytime.

I just dined there and ordered 3 dishes, Pasquale chopped salad, diavola pizza and lemon pasta. 

The service was very good and accommodating, filled water regularly. Checked in regularly.

The Food had good flavor overall, but was not that extraordinary for the prices. The pasta, in particular, was very small for the 24 dollar price tag.

The staff was attentive and the service was great. I ordered the little neck clam pizza which also has broccoli rabe, cream & lemon. Let me just say that the pizza's taste was good but it was EXPENSIVE. It was $28. And for the size as well. I ate the whole pizza in one sitting (it was good, but it was also small).

So echoing what a bunch of reviews on here already stated - it's good but doesn't justify the steep price point.

Big fan of their sister restaurant, but was just soso on this one - everything was just ok and nothing special. Wine and cocktails were pretty basic and the pizza wasn't served hot like I wanted it to be. Salad was simple, but not in a wowing way - just bland. Roasted Brussels sprouts were soft and flavorless, not crispy at all! Service was good, but the food just didn't live up to the many great pizzerias in NYC for the price. Wouldn't come back. 

Follow me on instagram @eatenbysteph

The Pasquale Chopped Salad and the Spaghetti al Limone were delicious but our one complaint related to the Littleneck Clam Pizza which is a house specialty. A small 6 slice pie for $28 should have more than one minuscule clam on each slice. I thought I ordered a broccoli rabe cream sauce pie, not a littleneck clam pie. Big disappointment.

Adorable location in Nolita in Little Italy.  Great corner for patio dining and people watching.  The Unctuous handmade pastas  are perfectly sauced.  We had the bucatini carbonara with generous chunks of guanciale and the spaghetti Cacio e Pepe. Do not miss the perfect wood fired oven- charred thin pizza as only New York can make.  The combination of crisp and chew with salumi and provolone is unbelievable.  The wine pairing was genius as the wine steward suggested a light flavorful Beaujolais.  The nose was amazing and did I say it was a Beaujolais?  It held up to the Pizza Diavolo and had enough acidity for my Cacio e Pepe spaghetti.  We started with braised leeks that had a enough tang to cut the richness of the braising sauce and a crunch from the toasted walnuts.  The rich burrata was paired with the fragrant and tart Frog Hollow peaches from California.  It was excellent with the toasted baguette slices generously buttered.  The dessert was a light Fior di Latte gelato with shortbread and apricots.  It was light and not too sweet.  A perfect finish.  The meal made me want to linger and just savor the experience.

I saw an article saying this restaurant had the best clam pizza in NYC, so I was instantly intrigued. It holds up to that name! However I found the pizza too soupy, you can't eat it with your hands or else everything falls off. I tried some of the ricotta pasta as well and the portion was so small!

overpriced, food is ok, tiny wine pours. they pack the place so you can hear the tables next to you and servers bump your chairs bringing people food since the space is so tight for the amount of tables they put in. wouldnt come bcak, much better italian in nyc

Good food, great wine. I came here on a Sunday and  we able to get a table for indoor dining without a reservation. The manager/hostess was super nice and very attentive. Great service all around by the staff.

They had a wine special for bubbles so we took advantage of it. For food, we got the 36-Month Prosciutto & Melon and Market Zucchini pizza as appetizers. They did not disappoint. 

For my main entree, I got the spaghetti. It was ok. I think it could've used a little bit more sauce. But I cleared the plate which means it was still good.

Overall, good moment.

This place is DOPE. Already planning my next trip back. I recently got back from Italy and this transported me back -- prosciutto and melon, Neapolitan style pizza fresh out of the oven and made right in front of you, delicious pasta, and great wines by the glass. We sat at the chefs counter and watched as they spun the pizza dough, which was cool. Overall great vibe with old school rap.. I was Shazam-ing every other song. It's sort of hard to get a reservation so that's slightly annoying but we booked ours on Resy for 6pm Sunday just a day before.

run, don't walk. i had the absolute best dinner here last night for my birthday. yes the food was obviously incredible, but i wanna give a shout out to the STAFF. every single person was such an amazing part of our experience from the host to the bussers to the food runners- everyone was kind and professional and helpful. but our server eric was literally the best. i didn't want to leave because i had so much fun with him during our experience. this place is so awesome. i can't wait to go back!

Love the vibe in this place! I think the owner of Charlie Bird is the chef here as well. Rap music, great location, and incredibly fresh food. 

What we ordered:
Limone Pasta $21
Black Truffle $45

The limone pasta was my absolute favorite and what I looked forward to most. The pasta made in house was very fresh with the perfect amount of lemon/light cream for the sauce. 10/10

Black truffle pasta was priced pretty high and wasn't my favorite. Shaved black truffle was a nice touch but I couldn't really taste the truffle at all. Sometimes truffle is really rich tasting, but this was almost too light. A little drizzle of truffle oil would make this better. 7/10

I enjoyed my meal here a lot! We got the burrata app, two glasses of wine and a beer, the rigatoni amatriciana, and the Brussels pizza!

My only two complaints were that the pours were SO small on the wine. Teeny tiny and not cheap. Delicious wine though! And then I felt the pizza could've used a bit more salt.

I will totally come back though, definitely a fun spot with great ambiance and a fun parklet!

Every single dish was pretty much fabulous. Great wine list. Music and vibe are perfect for date night, girls night, fun night with friends. Yes I liked the clam pizza but their pastas were my favorite - perfectly Al dente and packed with umami!

Love myself some good pizza and pasta. This place has a limited menu, but has lots of different good options. I split the pizza and pasta with my dinner date and it was perfect! The pizza was cooked just right and the pasta was not over sauced. Overall, I would suggest to anyone!  It made for a great date night. I suggest making a reservation because they get very busy. Outdoor seating does not have heaters so it is not ideal as we approach colder weather.

Ok let me start that the winner here is the staff. Our waiter knew his stuff about the menu/wine list, was incredibly friendly, and well attentive. My main meh was that tables are genuinely an inch apart so beyond the uneasiness of covid you are genuinely in the next tables conversation. We were surprised that there were no cocktails, or alcoholic spritz. The menu is small but has good options. The food was genuinely very good but just expensive for what it was.

First timer at this establishment. Traffic caused us to be late so we called ahead and they were accommodating and gave us later time so thank you! The food was good. We had the burrata, it's burrata can't go wrong anywhere. Had the little neck clam pizza and it was ok, could've had more toppings to be honest.. and the Bucatini all'Amatriciana, which was really good but the portion was really small.
The ambiance was nice and cozy but little loud.

The good: friendly greeting when entered, good vibe/music/"scene," and the enclosed patio was very warm, as good as sitting inside.  Water refills were fast.
Service was perfunctory, not amazing, and after our food was delivered we never saw our server again. I think the host brought us the bill.  We were not told if there were specials?
The bad: food was slow to come out ( they were packed) and the pasta tasted fine but the portions were like an appetizer size, especially for the price. This is just pasta- no reason to not give a few extra forkfuls to make it a decent portion. Our 2 pizzas were BURNT. I know what wood fired and leparding is supposed to be- this was black all over. As soon as they were delivered I looked at them and thought how could you send this order out? I waited to say something until we tried it and our whole party agreed it was way overdone with the bottom of both pies completely burned black and stiff like a cracker- but nobody ever returned to the table to check on us for us to say anything. We left hungry and had to walk to another restaurant and order more food, because we did not want to eat anything else at Pasquale Jones.  Also we ate on the heated patio but the indoor restaurant is packed in so tightly the center tables may as well be communal. If you care about distancing this will not be the place for you. They have every square inch used for seating and it is on top of one another. Found the meal unimpressive, especially for the cost.

The restaurant is a shadow of its former self. Used to live a few blocks away and go here all the time. Have eaten here twice in the last 3 months. The food has gone down in quality (e.g., I had to hunt for clams on my clam pizza). Also had a delivery from here, and little cost cutting things (e.g., no longer deliver in an oven-safe container to crisp crust, ordered a glass bottle of soda and got a can). Sad to see the quality level slide.

This place was amazing! The service was very attentive and kind and super efficient. Here's what to get and I recommend all the following: 
1. Burrata app
2. Clam pizza - this was fire
3. The Diavola pizza

All really good, if I had to pick one I would take the clam pizza first. Order a bottle of wine, and you have yourself an amazing dinner experience. Interior is beautiful and service was great. Highly recommend!

Came here with a few girlfriends and had a great dinner. Only downfall was no cocktails, and an expensive wine menu but the food was worth it.

We got the clam pizza, burrata pizza, anchovy bucatini, and burrata starter. While I think they might be known for pizza (rightfully so) do not sleep on the pasta. I think the bucatini was my favorite item we ordered but everything was great!

Service was attentive. The pasta we ordered was split up into two bowls for us to share but it was SO incredibly salty that I had stop eating it and wasted half of it. The clam pizza hardly had any clam pieces and was also burnt in several places that made the pizza overwhelmingly taste bad. Depending on where you're seated, it was cool seeing the food being prepared.

Amazing service and out of this world food. Everything is so fresh and delicious it's hard to describe. The manager is also amazing and gave us the best wine pairing with our food. The desserts weren't on the menu but definitely worth saving some room for with an adffogato. The truffle pizza is a must have before the season is over, we will definitely be back to have it again. I don't think I can go back to regular Italian food after eating here lol. Can't wait to go back!

Just an ok experience. While this might be a trendy go to spot it missed the mark with me. Overpriced, not a lot of options, didn't accommodate my request for a vegan meal and the staff was less than welcoming plus we ate outside in an enclosed area with not enough heat while 17 degrees outside. If asked to go again? No thank you, I will just pass. I left hungry!

Food (2/5), Ambiance (4/5), Service (4/5)

SEATING / AMBIANCE
This restaurant has indoor and enclosed patio seating available. The enclosed patio seating is covered, but the seats are placed so tightly together that there is not much wiggle room between you and the seat behind you. The inside is dimly lit and romantic, while the outside is beautiful for watching the sunset 

FOOD
Too incredibly salty. My friend and I struggled to finish our pasta because if this. Would highly not recommend if you're looking for high quality pasta as Little Italy is just a block down

SERVICE
Our server was attentive and came by to check on us at just the right times. 

Overall, wouldn't dine here again

The food here is quite good.  The pasta dishes, except one of the Lemone Pasta are house made.  the Lemone is smoked.  Starters such as the leeks and Pasquale chopped are good.  the Cavaatelli and Lemone pasta are hits, as was the stripped bass.  We enjoyed the olive oil cake.  If you love olive oil you will love this desert.

Wildly disappointed in the pizza. The crust was completely charred and inedible. I shared the pie with one other person and neither of us could eat any of the crust. While the pizza was decent (perhaps a little too wet), we left over 25% of the meal because it was inedible. Upon telling the waitress about my disappointment, (the same waitress who said when we first sat down, "just tell me what you want...I got you") her response was "well that's the way we do it here, but I'll tell the chef." I did see other pies come out looking exactly the same, so I believe the waitress was telling the truth. Plus if you read the other pizza reviews, the same complaint has been made more than once. Therefore, the only reason I gave this restaurant 2 stars and not 1, is because the pasta dish I tasted was really, really good. The noise level and the crowded tables is not my favorite environment, but could be okay if not being able to hear your companions easily and bumping into tables and moving waiters on your way to the bathroom doesn't bother you.

My family walk in today at 5:15pm.. we immediately were  turn away saying they had no available tables  . I Checked their reservation app and you could make reservation at 5:30 pm and 6 pm. I guess this restaurants and pick choose their customers. Beware family's not welcomed.

I ate here this weekend -- the restaurant was half empty and there were 5-6 waiters just standing around, and tons of tables waiting an hour+ for their food.

I ordered a pizza and pasta and the food took nearly 2 hours to come out -- and we had to flag down the staff multiple times to remind them about our order, which the kitchen forgot about multiple times.

Food was decent, but the wait time for just a regular pizza and pasta is way too long, especially considering the fact that it wasn't even busy

Overall a 2/5 and I would not return. The restaurant is giving ~out of touch vibes~

Service was weird - they had over 10 hosts/servers standing around waiting to clear our plates the moment we finished. They changed our silverware 2x before any food came to our table.

Our food still took over an hour & came out in waves so we didn't all eat at same time. When we asked where the rest of the food was they urged us to order  an additional appetizer because the pizza oven would "take a while." Pasta was decent, definitely a bit too salty & pizza crust was burnt. Super overpriced- $30 for a personal sized pizza? Not worth it. They charged us $6 for bread for the table - which is a bit tacky in my opinion!

They make good pizza, but a nightmare to order delivery. First time we ordered the Pizza arrived completely cold. Second time, they confirmed the order at 8:36pm, then when the Doordash driver went to pick it up at 9:20pm they cancelled the order. Worst experience I have had with a restaurant in the city.

Delicious food!!! The service was super friendly and the flavors were delightful. The design of the restaurant overall was beautiful with lots of little details from the silverware to the glasses and the tables. I really liked both pastas we tried. The clam pizza was delightful too. Would highly recommend.
Amanda, the manager, was incredibly rude, and would not do anything when servers were rude. The worst service of any restaurant in the city
Fantastic food, amazing service, wonderful ambience. Wait staff is attentive and courteous. Their new(ish) mushroom tagliatelle is a must try!
Excellent restaurant.  The staff and Amanda the manager are wonderful.   We plan on going back to this restaurant very soon

We were really underwhelmed with the food here. Great service which is really why it's a 2. 

Overall everything was lacking a lot of flavor. We started with the leeks which were solid. 

We ordered two pastas, one with mushrooms and the lumache. Now I love a good Al dente pasta, but these were both quite underdone. 

The clam pizza and half chicken were good, again just could have used more flavor. 

Overall, could not justify the quality and taste of the food with the price.
Great atmosphere, friendly staff and lots of fun.  I only wish that they would have some Glutten free options.
Great food and great service! Isaiah was the best waiter - so kind and fun! We'll definitely be back!

If you are reading this GO SOMEWHERE ELSE!

Food is fine - not bad but not good - but the service, price, and atmosphere is atrocious. Extremely overpriced (even for NYC), and took over 2 hours for our entrees!! We were still waiting on 1 more entree towards the end of dinner when we just said this is absurd and enough and decided to get the check and leave.

There are so many better restaurants in the area and NYC in general. We actually went to Nolita Pizza right next door after (since, also, the portions were extremely small and we left hungry) and the pizza was delicious and inexpensive - many times better than PJ's pizza to be honest.

Skip this POS!

I am honestly just leaving this review to hopefully save someone money on an overpriced and not-worth-it meal. 

I've tried giving this place multiple chances, although their service is great, I always have the worst experience with their food. The last 2 times I've eaten there for dinner, I have been queasy in bed by the end of the night. And the last time I went a couple weeks ago, the pasta was so undercooked that the noodles were crunchy and hurt my tooth.... They also did not even offer to take it off the bill. Not to mention they have also increased their pricing and decreased portion sizes. 

I live in soho/little Italy area and I can assure you that there are so many other quality pasta places in the area that are worth a visit.

Overall - food is good, but overpriced, ambience is nice with a chic casual crowd, service is a little too attentive. 

Came here with a couple of friends to catch up on a lovely summer evening.  We sat outside so we could relax and chat for a while.  

Was disappointed that they didn't have any cocktails - so ordered a glass of wine.  Wine Is around $20 a glass.

We had the crudo appetizer $25 - thought that it would be a nice plate with some thinly sliced hamachi.  The crude came out and all of us laughed.  The plate was the size of an ashtray - we thought that it was an amuse bouche coming out.  It was delicious but there were only 7 pieces of quarter sized pieces of hamachi. 

The roasted tomato pasta and lemon pasta were both delicious.  Portions were small - like a half sized portion.   

The clam pizza was only okay - lots of burnt parts and not enough sauce or pieces clam to be noteworthy. 

We ordered some focaccia - this was delicious with a roasted red pepper spread. 

For dessert it was a pistachio gelato with shortbread crumble and roasted strawberries.  It sounded so good, but it was disappointing. This was so-so - no pistachio flavor, roasted strawberries tasted more burnt than sweet.  

Would come back if my friends wanted to, but wouldn't seek it out again.

It was... fine. Super nice waitstaff, good location but your outside seating is on a super busy and noisy street (part of the convenient location package). Food was just ok. There's better places in the area. Fun fact, one of our party accidentally dropped a fork and a passerby scooped it up. Free fork? Sorry management - we didn't grab it fast enough.

Sit at the counter! It is seriously so fun. My friend and I came here on a whim on a Saturday night. We had the best service. We go the pasta special and a pizza to share, both were amazing. When we said we were too full for dessert, the chef sent some out anyway. The ambiance is great. Will definitely be back.
Nice restaurant, food was above average but sitting outside in the "makeshift" stalls ...was the worst experience!  Rather stay home...but no seats available inside!

I haven't ever left a review on Yelp, but I guess I'm starting now. Was excited to have a nice dinner with family that rarely is in the same place all at once, and was met with a disappointing experience. Halfway into appetizers, they came to "change plates for the next course". Except we had plenty left to enjoy? Everyone got their plates except for me. I had to wait a while before I could finally flag down someone to bring me a plate so I could finish eating them. Was told when I asked for one that they did not give me a plate because I ordered pasta for my main (?). What does that have to do with finishing the three appetizers we ordered? The pasta was good (needed salt) but the pizza has gone downhill. Wasn't sure why people thought this pizza was amazing in the first place, but it has certainly gone downhill unfortunately. The cherry on top was when a member of the staff came around to ask us to leave after 1 hr and 45 minutes when the reservation said nothing initially about a time limit. We ordered a $200 bottle of wine that we had to finish. Epic fail. I know this place is on some list about best pizza outside of Italy but for someone who has been there, DON'T WASTE YOUR MONEY.
Amazing food. Fantastic service. Great atmosphere! They can accommodate vegans even if menu doesn't at first seem vegan friendly!

Came to Pasquale Jones for a friend's birthday as a group of 6. It is quite a small space, but the ambiance is great for a pre night out dinner. Dimly lit, loud music, it's definitely a vibe... went from 3 stars to 4 for this. This space is wine and beer only, so if you're hoping for cocktails, go elsewhere. We opted for a bottle of white and shared everything. Food was quite good, my favorite was the amantriciana pasta. Pizza was good, though I was expecting a bit more in terms of taste. I'm all for wood fired, though it seemed a bit too charred to me. If I had to choose my favorite, it was the brussels sprouts. On the pricier side for what you are getting, but again, it's a trendy spot so you're paying for the vibe. Service was great, no complaints there!
Cozy, romantic vibes, excellent service and food! The menu is seasonal-- we got the burrata, clam pizza and pasta with uni. Will be back!

This review is based solely on customer service - not the quality of food.

I went to dinner at Pasquale Jones with three other friends at the end of October. I ended up taking the largest portion of the tab ($250) - and the others split the rest of the bill (which ended up being about $45 each). Because I took the majority of the bill, I did NOT tip on my $250, but rather had everyone else take care of the 20% tip, as I was expensing my portion. 

Well, I got my card statement a few days later and found that I was charged $268 - which is interesting because I KNOW I crossed out the tip line and wrote very clearly $250 in the total line. So it's obvious that someone turned my 5 into a 6, and the 0 into an 8 to add an $18 tip on top of what was already tipped by everyone else. 

I tried to call as soon as I saw this - giving them the benefit of the doubt - but they don't have a phone number you can call. Instead, they texted me and after letting them know what had happened, they told me it must have been an error by the person who input the final bill (lol - sure) and that they would be refunding me only the $18 they overcharged me.

Well - it's now a full 1.5 months later. I've followed up twice. I've never seen a refund. I've told them I'm planning to file it as fraud with my credit card - just wanted to let everyone else know about the scam they're running. Make sure to check your receipts if you dare to dine there - they'll be happy to steal your money!

Was excited to eat here!  Unfortunately the pizzas we ordered were all undercooked.  The dough was too chewy/soft.  I was shocked when I read through the wine list.  Almost impossible to find anything under $200.  The appetizers were really good not great.  The staff were standoffish more interested in talking amongst themselves than being engaged with guests.  Will not come back.

We had Friday evening reservations for 4 people, and overall our experience was very poor. We were seated at the outdoor "heated" patio (what our reservation was for). The space itself was very tight and did not feel like it was heated at all. The lemon tree decor was pretty.

Our waiter appeared to be very attentive at the start, but we quickly realized he was there to upsell us on everything. We were given tap water (more on this later) and chose a bottle of wine to share. The wine list itself was not well curated, as it did not have enough wines at each price point. I would guess about 75% of the wines were over $200. When the waiter came to take our wine order, he said the bottle we chose was not available, but that he had another bottle of the same type that would cost $5 more (and was not on the actual wine list). Out of principal, we kindly asked if he could sub that bottle for the same price and he declined. We ordered the bottle anyway.

In terms of the food and wine experience, the wine was served a bit too cold, and the waiter did not open the bottle in front of us (typically a huge red flag for wine service). We ordered two pasta dishes and two pizzas (the clamshell and the margherita). One of the pastas came out within 10 minutes of ordering, and the two pizzas came out a full 10 minutes after that. The 2nd pasta dish never came out at all, and the waiter didn't acknowledge it until we asked him where it was. I can't speak for the first pasta dish or clamshell pizza, but the margherita pizza left a lot to be desired. The wood fired aspect was too overdone and took away from the actual taste of the pizza almost to the point where it felt like we were eating ashes. 

The manager did eventually come to the table and offer his apologies about the 2nd pasta dish and gave us the option to have it brought out (and take it off the bill). However, at that point, we didn't want to wait and declined. 

The waiter brought out our check and the 2nd pasta dish that never came was left off of it. However, the restaurant charged us a $2 per person fee for "filtered" tap water. This was mentioned with an asterisk on the bottom of the menu, but we had assumed that would have been a buy up option. The waiter should have been more forthcoming about that. Overall, we had a very poor dining experience and would certainly not recommend this place.

Pasquale Jones is a trendy Nolita Italian hot spot should be. The wine list is always a star and every course has dishes that just don't disappoint. The location is also perfect for hitting the town after a fun meal with friends. Come for date night, taking your parents out, or just because. You won't regret it! 

Need to know: quaint vibey Italian spot with consistently great menu & specials

Must order: Lemon pasta

I went with my BFF/Cousin on a Saturday night to enjoy some pizza and wine! We made reservations for the enclosed patio, however, when we arrived in time for our resy, they sat us on the outside patio. It was freezing and we let our server know right away like hey! We can't eat out here!  They were so packed but she gave us an option of bar seats if the couple that was seated left soon enough, we could take their bar seats. We accepted the offer and waited. Our champagne and first pizza came and it was good! The hot honey made the Sopressata  pie better so definitely drizzle that hot honey! We got lucky and the couple finally left so we got the bar seats!!! It was great and by that time  We  had the clam pie, My lordddddd was it delicious! A few more glasses of champagne later, I had the Pasta Al Limone and it was perfect. I can't find anything to complain about and the night was a GREAT. Ugh we had a blast and we willlll be back again!!!! It was also super fun watching the chefs at work and it was intense behind that counter ok?! It was great, Thanks for having us! 

The service was a lil missing after we got our bar seats but we actually enjoyed being left to chat and giggle off the champagne and watch the kitchen magic happening before our eyes, one of the front of house staff did get us extra napkins and refilled our glasses but that was towards the end. But we appreciated how kind he seemed and he did make us feel good. It was super laid back despite the pace of the scene behind the bar counter.

The music was off the chain ok!? WHOEVER is in charge of the music, esp on that Saturday night, Give them a raise! Ok? A RAISE.

I had heard great things about this place and was excited to try it when I had some family in town. Made a reservation for the outdoor patio and was seated right away, but was told that there was another reservation a few hours after us so we'd have to give up the table then. No issues there. The waiter was very friendly and attentive (almost too attentive, as he came by the table many times when we hadn't had a chance to review the menu). We are vegetarian so ordered the Brussel sprouts and focaccia to start (both good, the focaccia had a subtle lemon flavor which was unique). For the mains we ordered the Brussel sprout pizza which was a white pie (quite tasty) and also a pasta which the waiter offered to turn into a pasta pomodoro but it was basically pasta shells with very average red sauce. Was not impressed with that. For dessert we ordered the gelato with grilled pineapple which was also quite nice. What killed me was that they charged 2 bucks a person for WATER and you can call it filtered all you want but please don't charge for tap water, it's a basic commodity. Not sure if I'd go back given the number of stellar Italian places in the city but we still enjoyed our time, for the company and ambience.

Nice and trendy spot near in Nolita. Service was good and everyone was friendly.

Littleneck clam pizza is the popular menu. I enjoyed the chilly oil that was served with it. The pizza dough is thin and chewy which I loved.

Pasta noodle is nicely Al dente.

Squash & Burrata comes with nicely toasted bread and the squash is more of a purée.

Overall, nice vibe, good food and service.

Hands down the best carbonara I've ever had. Great staff, cozy, unpretentious... and the food is simple and perfect. Forget everyone hawking from restaurant doors to convince you they're the one true original Mulberry St. restaurant. These folks just worry about great food.

Went out with a girlfriend on a Friday night to Pasquale Jones and it was packed! The music was loud but had me dancing in my seat.

We shared the Ricotta, Spaghetti alla Limone, and Lumache (which was definitely our favorite).

The food was nothing special but the ambiance/vibes were great. Worth checking out once!
I've always wanted to try this place. The food was pretty average. I've had better and worse in the city. I wouldn't go out of your way but it's good.

I'm not sure why this place has 3.5 stars. I came here because I wanted to be close to where my event was happening, and it was a few blocks from the restaurant. I didn't make any reservations, so we can only sit outside in the enclosed patio or by the chefs counter. The chefs counter it was, and that's where you see all the action. It was great seeing them make the pizza's from scratch. The service was great. I didn't know who our server was as it was always a different person. But they were on top of everything. 

My friend and I decided to order pasta and pizza since that's their specialty. Got the diavola pizza that came with this sweet pepper on the side in a tiny bowl. The pizza was really tasty, I put some chili flakes on it for good measure. The pasta we got was called the Amatriciana, which was a tad bit expensive, I wouldn't get that again as it didn't meet the price point. The entire meal didn't make me stuffed, but it was enough to last me until lunch the next day.

food was great but the service was excellent! our server, Payton, went absolutely above and beyond give us an amazing time all based on a dessert joke! 
Sommeliers were super helpful and gave a great recommendation to pair and please everyone at the table. 
Thanks for an amazing time!!

We came here as a larger group and thought the food was ok. The pizza toppings kept sliding off of the pizza. We ordered a few bottles of wine and it was extremely expensive. Overall, the wine list although good felt like it had been dramatically overpriced. The bottles we ordered were around $200 per bottle and if buying at a store were around $35.

Came to Pasquale Jones for an early dinner on Saturday night. Ordered three dishes, my favorite one being the Pane Carasu with baked pita bread with whipped ricotta and honey. The Lumache pasta was good but not amazing, it needed some more salt in my opinion. The pizza was very good, thin crust but some areas were burned. Good vibe and music inside. And the waiter Tom was great!

I am in love with the braised leeks! Texture is soft with a little crunch from the walnuts. The flavor is subtle and quite frankly sublime.
We had two pizzas, one margarita which was um um good! Then the clam pizza which was expensive and you had to look hard to find clams. That was a drag. Why can't these restaurants figure out that being a little generous goes a long way. Clams at  25-50 cents a clam retail and of course you are buying at cost,  maybe just maybe you could put a generous amount of clams on the pie? Darn, it wouldn't break the bank.
At $30 for a smallish pie is not an unreasonable request.
It's a lovely atmosphere to be sure and other than the servers are jumping at the bit to take your plate away,  they am to please.  I for now will stick to the Margarita pie and the leeks.

Loveddddd the hamachi crudo, would 10/10 reccomend this dish!!! The spaghetti was light, lemony & yummy. The pizza was a good blend of flavors, I love a crispy pizza so wish it was a little more crispy but overall had a great flavor & loved the wood fired flavor. Went super late on a Saturday but the vibes were still great. Resy was very easy to quick last minute!!
Came here on a Saturday afternoon. Loved the braised leeks (I don't even normally eat leeks) and the mezza stellina. Was pretty quiet, and service was good.

I've been here twice- once around Christmastime and once during a terrible heat wave in late July. 

Our winter visit was intimate with delicious food and attentive service. The pasta was delicious, but portions are extremely small for the price (about half of what you would get anywhere else in the city). 

Recently, I made a reservation to dine inside, since it was about 90 degrees outside. A relative of mine wanted to return because of our positive experience in December. The host walked us directly outside since the restaurant was full. Service was significantly slower and food wasn't quite as good as I had remembered.

If anything, go for the ambiance in the colder months, but you can definitely find a better deal and a better meal elsewhere.
One of the best places in soho worth every possible moment. Great food and wonderful staff
Exactly what I'm looking for if I want sit down pizza and some pasta options. Great casual dining.

Pasquale Jones had been on my list for a while but since my husband has a gluten allergy we never got around to coming since the restaurant doesn't have that many gf options as it's mostly pizza and pasta other than a few appetizers.  I finally came with a friend though recently and overall I found the food to be good and well priced though small portions - we ordered the stracciatella, which was tasty though a little runny - would've been nice to have some bread to use, tortelli, which was good but a pretty small portion, it also had a hint of citrus that I wasn't expecting and we also shared the fairytale eggplant pizza which was delicious.  I'm glad I came and I'd go back if I was in the neighborhood. gemegmegmail

Ass don't go octopus was so bad and chewy they don't serve liquor and I'm pissed 
Fuck this

Firing on all cylinders this cozy corner Italian restaurant has some of the best authentic pizzas I've ever had. We were fortunate enough to get a reservation for two on Saturday night and we're promptly seated. They kindly found a bottle of Prosecco, which was not on the menu and  honored our request for a glass.
The menu has a really enticing list of vegetable appetizers salt with pastas and some meat courses as well but the pizza I believe is the star we had braves leaks which were cooked to perfection along with a lemon pasta. Where are you could taste all the subtle flavors in that. Lastly, we had a pie w pomodoro , anchovies  garlic and burrata added as it comes out of the oven , super bright flavorful .
Added some of Calabrian pepper oil for that extra splash of flavor.
Their personal pies are not to be handheld,This is a fork and knife pizza place, and the crust was cooked perfectly. They have a nice selection of wines and beers and the service was extremely attentive and helpful. 
Ambiance low light and intimate even if on the small side.
The food was great and the service was exceptional. The ambiance was nice. I would highly recommend.

Everything we had was first class from the chopped salad, the exquisitely dressed burrata, the clam pizza (sublime), the sausage pizza, and calzone. And their wine list and level of service are tops also. Can't wait to return. Thank you Pasquale !

Pasquale Jones was a really good vibe and dinner spot for a work outing. The food was good but not great. For the proximity to little Italy I was expecting a little bit more variety and flavor. I really liked the burrata and meat balls. The pizza fell a little flat on flavor but that's show biz baby. Overall a great spot for a dinner and a laugh with coworkers!

Walked into Pasquale Jones on a Friday night around 6:30pm and were seated immediately without a reservation. They have a number of indoor and outdoor tables and were about 50% full when we arrived. 

We ordered a few items, and everything was okay. What makes Pasquale Jones a 3-star in my book is value. We ordered a $20+ pasta (before tax and tip), which came in an extremely small portion and was only enough for each of us to have one small serving (approximately 5-6 pieces of pasta each for 3 people). We also got a pizza which was fine but again, quite pricey for what we got. Service was fine, albeit a bit pushy when it came to ordering. Ambiance at Pasquale was so-so; the space is modern and decorated well, but the tables are so close together and it gets quite loud inside.

Overall, Pasquale Jones has decent food, but the price points are just too high for me.

I went here for the first time last night after my son recommended it. I have very strict dietary needs, and I can honestly say that this is the first time I was taken care of so well and it resulted in a delicious meal. Usually when I eat out, I seriously have to compromise and have some plain protein and steamed vegetables. My meal was delicious! All of this happened because of my very caring and attentive waiter, McCabe. He advised me on one item which we decided on and then he went back and reconfirmed with the chef that it did not include anything that I could not have. He came back to me and said unfortunately, it wasn't going to work , and then they created something else for me that was fabulous! Everyone who takes care of people at a restaurant should care this much! He's truly an asset!

Super noisy. The good was good, but just good. They are VERY proud of their food and charge accordingly.

We'll make a different choice next time.

Cute cozy restaurant in Soho. I wanted to love it because I picked this place after watching a reel a good reviewer posted for my own birthday with best friend. 

Service was very charming with our cute waiter. 

1. Fish sashimi appetizer - very small but tastes fresh and good
2. Clam pizza- this was a big hit.  Very tasty and dough was soft and freshly made and thin - and it was very good 
3.  Beets Salad- beautifully made and tastes very good. 
4. Lemon pasta - very disappointing. Tasted really bad like a horse house. I was not sure what's going on.  Very small amount 
5.  Salad - very disappointing as too much dressing and very salty. Not eatanle. The salami tasted very old, and we left it almost untouched. A big dish. 

Overall, it was ok.   We didn't want to stay for dessert.
Pretty good food, good service. They're just over capacity with the outside tables and can't handle it. If you're okay with that then it's a fine experience, good ambiance.

Really cute outdoor area in the summer (reminded me of the European cafes). We liked it for a late afternoon post-shopping break. It's not an extensive menu but the pizza and arincini were delicious and perfect for an afternoon snack.

I'm not usually one to go to Italian restaurants but Pasquale Jones is the only restaurant that changes my mind. Their menu is fantastic and their setups work together so well. Last time I was there we ordered the hen of the woods mushrooms and mascarpone Ice cream both of which I can't stop thinking about. Their pizzas and leeks are a classic. I love to sit at the bar and watch the chefs work. A perfect go to delicious meal!
Phenomenal food and ambience. Liked all the pizza and pastas but the chicken really blew us away.

Have been here twice, a rare repeat for me (though it was out of my control). Between my first and second visits, roughly one year had passed. The menu was completely different. None of the pictures I had taken on my first visit matched menu items on my second visit. This is a good thing. This is a serious menu at a casual restaurant that blasts NYC classic rap.
Amazing service, amazing food & the perfect ambiance for date night! I can tell this place is properly managed because it seems to run like a well oiled machine! So happy I passed by.

Poor customer service. They don't answer their phones and no one gets back to you via text message. They were supposed to refund me for something and instead put the refund back on the wrong credit card and I'm still waiting for a manager or owner to take care of this matter for me several months later.

Overpriced and not great food and bad ambiance. Asked to add sausage to a margarita pizza and they couldn't ?? The shells pasta with lobster was so small and overpriced. Would avoid this restaurant especially in a city loaded with great pizza. Oh- cheapest bottle of wine was $125. Skip this place

Overall it was a great experience! The hostess allowed us to change our seats bc it was chilly outside. Seating is tight, but that's everywhere in NY. We sat at the bar which was so cool bc we got to watch them prepare and bake the pizzas. The meatballs are SO GOOD! we ordered the pizza with Brussels sprouts which wasn't my favorite but my husband enjoyed it. I would have gone for a simple pepperoni pie which looked really good. Would definitely go back!

Come here for the pizzas and the pizzas only... I came here for dinner specifically because my husband was craving pizza and the wait times were crrrazy as usual for a Friday night in SoHo. 

The hostess was kind of nice to rearrange for us to get seated during prime dinner time. We ordered the clam pizza that tasted fishy despite a healthy dose of lemon juice over it, what really complemented it well was their hot chili oil infused with loads of chili peppers. We also ordered another entree which should very well be an appetizer due to its shockingly small portion size for its high 20 something dollar price tag. Though our ragu was tasty it was definitely not worth it when we could've gotten something more filling such as another pizza. The waitress gave us a fair warning but will not be back given NYCS plethora of Italian restaurants. 

Another dampen to our dinner out was that a hobo was begging us for change as we were eating.

came here for a post work glass of wine. It is so incredibly noisy but was busy so I thought I would give it a try. The patrons were literally yelling over each other at the table to have a conversation. My glass of wine was about 3 ounces for $24. Here is a pic and I did not take a sip of it. Too loud and too expensive.

Food was good. The service, however, was absolutely terrible. Our reservation was at 8 and we sat promptly. Unfortunately, this was the only prompt service of the night. It's took close to 15 minutes for a server to come to our table. We had a question re the wine list which the server could not answer and advised that a sommelier would come and assist. About 15 minutes later (30 minutes since we were sat), a sommelier finally came over to answer a simple question. We ordered a bottle and proceeded to wait about 10 mins for the sommelier to come back and present the bottle. After approving the bottle, the sommelier took the bottle away to open it at the host stand. I watched as the sommelier placed our open bottle on the host stand, become distracted, and walk away. About 45 minutes after sitting, we finally got the wine and placed our food order. This was the last time we saw the waitress. We spent the rest of the evening flagging down support staff trying to get attended to. What was most frustrating was that we could see the servers standing in the service station chatting as well as standing at the host stand doing to same. As I said, the food was pretty good, but not worth the hassle of the service. If the service was even decent, this place would be worth the price.  Based on our experience, I  recommend going elsewhere to spend your money.

Great food and service. My favorite pizza in NY and the Chicken Saltimbocca was the best chicken dish I've ever eaten. Everything else we ordered was delicious as well. Great service and fun atmosphere

4.5 stars
The Pasquale Jones restaurant was the venue for a family birthday celebration for 6.  It is located in hip and trendy Soho and it is certainly in its correct element.   There is an open kitchen and we were seated in a curved banquet. The menu is streamlined with Pizzas, small plates, salads, pastas, and a handful of entrees, plus sides. There is a pizza oven on site and service is aware and very strong. This is a serious restaurant and all items were cooked or prepared to perfection. It was pricey but the quality is evident. 
The littleneck clam pizzas with Broccoli Rabe, Cream & Lemon were a hit as was the  DIAVOLA Pizza with Salumi Napoletano, Provolone Picante & Mint. A single meatball was excellent.  

THE TAGLIATELLE BOLOGNESE With Heritage Pork, Veal, & Parmigiano was as fresh as can be. A snide hamburger helper for grown-ups comparison was just a snarky joke.  We scored the final Diet Coke and skipped desserts.  
An occasional visit to a restaurant with beautiful décor, sharp service, and cutting edge food preparation is a special treat so kudos to the team at this establishment.
This should be rated higher - great service, food and ambiance. Crudo, beets and pumpkin pizza were particular highlights for us
Amazing local Italian restaurant, I enjoy it every time! Great wine list as well. Everything was awesome.
